programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc:
Chris and Lee travel to Eton Wick to help Andrew and Angela revive their Victorian cottage garden. Once lovingly maintained, it has now fallen into neglect, with a rotten pergola, a decaying arbour seat and overgrown borders in need of care. The uneven, rough surface also makes the garden unsafe and inaccessible for their young son William.
Andrew and Angela dream of putting their own twist on a traditional Victorian cottage garden with timeless tranquillity and modern functionality. They want to create a beautiful, low-maintenance space that’s also accessible for William, who relies on outdoor time because of his disabilities. The garden will feature smooth, accessible pathways, strategic seating areas and a calming, interactive play zone designed with William’s mobility in mind. A secluded corner filled with soothing plants and comfortable seating will offer the family a place to unwind and reconnect after hospital visits and busy days.
Andrew and Angela met while on holiday in Dublin and have shared a love of travel ever since. Angela, originally from America, and Andrew, a seasoned world traveller himself, settled down when she became pregnant, buying their home to start a family. But life soon took an unexpected turn when their son William was born prematurely with a rare condition, bilateral tibial hemimelia, causing severe malformations in both legs and feet. Their renovation plans were put on hold as hospital visits, surgeries and recoveries became part of everyday life. Earlier this year, William underwent an amputation of his right leg and is now learning to walk confidently with his prosthetic. Three further surgeries on his left leg are planned, with more likely into his early twenties.
Despite these challenges, Andrew and Angela remain optimistic and determined to create a safe, tranquil and joyful outdoor space where William can play and the family can relax together.
Can Chris and Lee craft a Victorian haven garden, one that blends charm, accessibility and serenity, on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Rose Ayling-Ellis came to fame on EastEnders and captured the nation’s hearts when she won Strictly. Since then, she’s used her platform to campaign for deaf rights. Now, Rose goes in search of her family history. She’s heard a rumour of Italian ancestry on her father’s side and is hoping for a bit of drama on her mum’s.
Rose starts by visiting her mum in Kent. Rose’s mum has an intriguing picture of Rose’s three-time great-grandmother. The family story is that she ran a pub in Birmingham with an iron fist. But Rose’s mum doesn’t know her name or if any of the stories are true. To find out, Rose heads to Birmingham.
Local historian Simon Briercliffe helps Rose put a name to her three-time great-grandmother – Agnes Chilton. Trade directories and census returns show that Agnes and her husband Alfred ran a pub. A local newspaper article tells a story worthy of an EastEnders plotline: Agnes and Alfred were caught up in an altercation with a customer, resulting in a court appearance. Rose discovers that Alfred died aged 48, leaving Agnes a widow. Fearing the worst for a woman on her own at that time, Rose is happy to discover that shortly after Alfred’s death Agnes moved to her own pub, the Aston Tavern.
Rose heads there to meet historian Professor Julie-Marie Strange and discovers that Agnes married again at the age of 50. However, two years later, Agnes’s second husband also died. Once again, Agnes was undeterred and expanded the pub further. Rose is delighted to find out that the current landlord of the Aston Tavern has named the rooms after former landlords, including Agnes. As Rose goes to find the room named after her ancestor, she reflects on what a resilient woman Agnes was.
Rose then turns to the paternal side of the family. At her dad’s house in Somerset, Rose’s grandma tells her that her father, Rose’s great-grandad, came from a huge family of 17 children. She doesn’t know a lot about them but remembers that her grandfather, James Welland, Rose’s great-great-grandad, lost his hand in an accident, and she also recalls her dad telling her that when he was a child, they were very poor and lived in a squat in Exeter. Rose also asks about the Italian connection. Rose’s dad explains that this story came through his dad’s side of the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads west to the seaside town of Aberystwyth, famous for its Victorian pier and unpredictable weather. Battling the rain are mother-and-son duo Margaret and Endaf, both hoping their shared love of a bargain will translate into serious profit for charity.
With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they’re paired with expert thrifters and sent racing around Aberystwyth’s charity shops. Endaf starts strongly, snapping up a quality blazer for under a tenner before confidently adding crystal glasses and rare Babycham glasses to his haul. He later spots a vintage wool-and-cashmere jacket, Joanna’s pick of the day, and takes a chance on a violin, proving he is willing to think outside the box.
Margaret, meanwhile, wastes no time securing her upcycle item – a nest of dark wood tables bought for just £3. She also picks up Dutch wooden clogs, a vintage leather messenger bag and gambles on an expensive suede jacket, carefully selecting items she believes have strong resale appeal. The contest has a warm but competitive family dynamic, with playful rivalry building between mum and son as the clock ticks down.
At the transformation stage, Endaf’s plain 80s leather jacket is dramatically reworked with fabric paint and new gold hardware by upcycle entrepreneur Emma Deeks, turning it into a bold statement piece. Margaret’s modest £3 tables are transformed by using a poured-paint technique, creating a colourful, marbled finish that completely reinvents them.
Then comes the live-streamed auction. Endaf grows in confidence as he pitches his items, using detail and humour to drive bids higher, especially on the vintage Burton jacket and his upcycled leather piece. Margaret charms viewers with her warmth and storytelling, successfully selling her clogs and making a strong profit on her upcycled tables.
When the totals are combined with their online sales, who will win between mother and son? The real triumph is for their chosen charity, the British Heart Foundation, with an impressive amount raised in total.
Rain-soaked, good-humoured and full of personality, this contest is a heartwarming family face-off that proves thrifting talent might just run in the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to Bridgend as the show brings its charity shop challenge to south Wales. With just 60 minutes on the clock and £100 each, best friends Anum and Betti go head-to-head to see who can turn second-hand bargains into the biggest profit for charity.
Paired with expert thrifters Pete and Lola, the race begins across Bridgend’s high street, where hidden gems lurk among the rails and shelves. Anum is drawn to vintage bric-a-brac and collectibles, snapping up teapots, crockery and curios, while Betti focuses on fashion, spotting bold fabrics, statement pieces and high-end labels.
But not every bargain is what it seems. Early excitement over a Burberry outfit raises questions about authenticity, while a pair of striking Christian Louboutin trainers presents a serious dilemma – a potential goldmine or a costly mistake. With the clock ticking and budgets shrinking, both teams must decide how much risk they are willing to take.
Once the shopping frenzy ends, attention turns to transformation. Each contestant chooses one item to be upcycled by expert makers. Betti’s nursery curtains are reworked into a stylish wrap dress, while Anum’s plain wooden jewellery box is transformed into a vibrant, hand-painted statement piece, proving that creativity can dramatically boost value.
Then comes the ultimate test: the live-streamed auction. Nerves are jangling as Anum and Betti step into the spotlight, pitching their items to a live online audience. As bids rise and fall in real time, confidence and charm become just as important as the items themselves. Authenticity checks deliver last-minute twists, and a risky gamble could either decide the winner or wipe out a chunk of their budget.
By the end of a dramatic auction, the profits are counted, surprises are revealed, and one contestant emerges ahead. But the real winner is charity, with all proceeds donated to the contestants’ chosen causes.
Packed with jeopardy, big decisions and satisfying transformations, the visit to Bridgend is a lively, feel-good episode that celebrates second-hand style, creative thinking and the thrill of finding hidden value where others might not look.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc:
Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die.
As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated.
Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death.
Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales.
Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the creative heart of Hebden Bridge – a former mill town famed for its independent spirit and as a filming location for the BBC TV series Happy Valley.
Today’s competitors are friends Emma and Sophie, who first met on a fashion shoot for Dove House Hospice. Now they’re going head-to-head to raise as much money as possible for the charity that brought them together. Guiding them are expert vintage thrifters – and husbands – Tom and Terry.
The teams quickly reveal very different shopping styles. Sophie and Tom dive straight into the nearest shop, where Sophie’s love of oversized menswear leads her to a vintage St Michael jacket – a nostalgic find with added appeal thanks to its 'Made in the UK' label. Emma and Terry take a steadier approach, carefully assessing a rare red rotary dial telephone before building a collection packed with retro charm.
The hunt for Joanna’s pick of the day – an original 1970s Holly Hobbie doll – adds extra jeopardy. While Tom hesitates over the gamble, Sophie trusts her instinct and pushes to secure the collectable toy. As time slips away, Emma and Terry uncover a colourful 1960s picnic set and an eye-catching Murano-style glass duck that divides opinion but promises personality at auction.
For the upcycling challenge, creativity takes centre stage. Emma selects a vintage rocking chair and plans to re-cover it using fabric from animal-illustrated curtains – a bold, characterful refresh. Sophie, however, leaves her upcycle decision perilously late, eventually opting for an unexpected sleeping bag with plans to transform it into a statement padded coat.
The final minutes are frantic for Sophie and Tom, who scramble to spend the remainder of their budget. With Joanna urging them on, they squeeze in a last-second dash for additional vintage finds before they run out of time.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must swap browsing rails for the rostrum. Emma channels calm confidence, while Sophie leans into theatrical flair. With bids climbing and pride on the line, it’s a spirited showdown, but whatever the outcome, Dove House Hospice stands to benefit from a creative, chaotic and thoroughly entertaining day on Hebden Bridge's high street.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc:
Chris and Lee travel to Eton Wick to help Andrew and Angela revive their Victorian cottage garden. Once lovingly maintained, it has now fallen into neglect, with a rotten pergola, a decaying arbour seat and overgrown borders in need of care. The uneven, rough surface also makes the garden unsafe and inaccessible for their young son William.
Andrew and Angela dream of putting their own twist on a traditional Victorian cottage garden with timeless tranquillity and modern functionality. They want to create a beautiful, low-maintenance space that’s also accessible for William, who relies on outdoor time because of his disabilities. The garden will feature smooth, accessible pathways, strategic seating areas and a calming, interactive play zone designed with William’s mobility in mind. A secluded corner filled with soothing plants and comfortable seating will offer the family a place to unwind and reconnect after hospital visits and busy days.
Andrew and Angela met while on holiday in Dublin and have shared a love of travel ever since. Angela, originally from America, and Andrew, a seasoned world traveller himself, settled down when she became pregnant, buying their home to start a family. But life soon took an unexpected turn when their son William was born prematurely with a rare condition, bilateral tibial hemimelia, causing severe malformations in both legs and feet. Their renovation plans were put on hold as hospital visits, surgeries and recoveries became part of everyday life. Earlier this year, William underwent an amputation of his right leg and is now learning to walk confidently with his prosthetic. Three further surgeries on his left leg are planned, with more likely into his early twenties.
Despite these challenges, Andrew and Angela remain optimistic and determined to create a safe, tranquil and joyful outdoor space where William can play and the family can relax together.
Can Chris and Lee craft a Victorian haven garden, one that blends charm, accessibility and serenity, on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Rose Ayling-Ellis came to fame on EastEnders and captured the nation’s hearts when she won Strictly. Since then, she’s used her platform to campaign for deaf rights. Now, Rose goes in search of her family history. She’s heard a rumour of Italian ancestry on her father’s side and is hoping for a bit of drama on her mum’s.
Rose starts by visiting her mum in Kent. Rose’s mum has an intriguing picture of Rose’s three-time great-grandmother. The family story is that she ran a pub in Birmingham with an iron fist. But Rose’s mum doesn’t know her name or if any of the stories are true. To find out, Rose heads to Birmingham.
Local historian Simon Briercliffe helps Rose put a name to her three-time great-grandmother – Agnes Chilton. Trade directories and census returns show that Agnes and her husband Alfred ran a pub. A local newspaper article tells a story worthy of an EastEnders plotline: Agnes and Alfred were caught up in an altercation with a customer, resulting in a court appearance. Rose discovers that Alfred died aged 48, leaving Agnes a widow. Fearing the worst for a woman on her own at that time, Rose is happy to discover that shortly after Alfred’s death Agnes moved to her own pub, the Aston Tavern.
Rose heads there to meet historian Professor Julie-Marie Strange and discovers that Agnes married again at the age of 50. However, two years later, Agnes’s second husband also died. Once again, Agnes was undeterred and expanded the pub further. Rose is delighted to find out that the current landlord of the Aston Tavern has named the rooms after former landlords, including Agnes. As Rose goes to find the room named after her ancestor, she reflects on what a resilient woman Agnes was.
Rose then turns to the paternal side of the family. At her dad’s house in Somerset, Rose’s grandma tells her that her father, Rose’s great-grandad, came from a huge family of 17 children. She doesn’t know a lot about them but remembers that her grandfather, James Welland, Rose’s great-great-grandad, lost his hand in an accident, and she also recalls her dad telling her that when he was a child, they were very poor and lived in a squat in Exeter. Rose also asks about the Italian connection. Rose’s dad explains that this story came through his dad’s side of the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads west to the seaside town of Aberystwyth, famous for its Victorian pier and unpredictable weather. Battling the rain are mother-and-son duo Margaret and Endaf, both hoping their shared love of a bargain will translate into serious profit for charity.
With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they’re paired with expert thrifters and sent racing around Aberystwyth’s charity shops. Endaf starts strongly, snapping up a quality blazer for under a tenner before confidently adding crystal glasses and rare Babycham glasses to his haul. He later spots a vintage wool-and-cashmere jacket, Joanna’s pick of the day, and takes a chance on a violin, proving he is willing to think outside the box.
Margaret, meanwhile, wastes no time securing her upcycle item – a nest of dark wood tables bought for just £3. She also picks up Dutch wooden clogs, a vintage leather messenger bag and gambles on an expensive suede jacket, carefully selecting items she believes have strong resale appeal. The contest has a warm but competitive family dynamic, with playful rivalry building between mum and son as the clock ticks down.
At the transformation stage, Endaf’s plain 80s leather jacket is dramatically reworked with fabric paint and new gold hardware by upcycle entrepreneur Emma Deeks, turning it into a bold statement piece. Margaret’s modest £3 tables are transformed by using a poured-paint technique, creating a colourful, marbled finish that completely reinvents them.
Then comes the live-streamed auction. Endaf grows in confidence as he pitches his items, using detail and humour to drive bids higher, especially on the vintage Burton jacket and his upcycled leather piece. Margaret charms viewers with her warmth and storytelling, successfully selling her clogs and making a strong profit on her upcycled tables.
When the totals are combined with their online sales, who will win between mother and son? The real triumph is for their chosen charity, the British Heart Foundation, with an impressive amount raised in total.
Rain-soaked, good-humoured and full of personality, this contest is a heartwarming family face-off that proves thrifting talent might just run in the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to Bridgend as the show brings its charity shop challenge to south Wales. With just 60 minutes on the clock and £100 each, best friends Anum and Betti go head-to-head to see who can turn second-hand bargains into the biggest profit for charity.
Paired with expert thrifters Pete and Lola, the race begins across Bridgend’s high street, where hidden gems lurk among the rails and shelves. Anum is drawn to vintage bric-a-brac and collectibles, snapping up teapots, crockery and curios, while Betti focuses on fashion, spotting bold fabrics, statement pieces and high-end labels.
But not every bargain is what it seems. Early excitement over a Burberry outfit raises questions about authenticity, while a pair of striking Christian Louboutin trainers presents a serious dilemma – a potential goldmine or a costly mistake. With the clock ticking and budgets shrinking, both teams must decide how much risk they are willing to take.
Once the shopping frenzy ends, attention turns to transformation. Each contestant chooses one item to be upcycled by expert makers. Betti’s nursery curtains are reworked into a stylish wrap dress, while Anum’s plain wooden jewellery box is transformed into a vibrant, hand-painted statement piece, proving that creativity can dramatically boost value.
Then comes the ultimate test: the live-streamed auction. Nerves are jangling as Anum and Betti step into the spotlight, pitching their items to a live online audience. As bids rise and fall in real time, confidence and charm become just as important as the items themselves. Authenticity checks deliver last-minute twists, and a risky gamble could either decide the winner or wipe out a chunk of their budget.
By the end of a dramatic auction, the profits are counted, surprises are revealed, and one contestant emerges ahead. But the real winner is charity, with all proceeds donated to the contestants’ chosen causes.
Packed with jeopardy, big decisions and satisfying transformations, the visit to Bridgend is a lively, feel-good episode that celebrates second-hand style, creative thinking and the thrill of finding hidden value where others might not look.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc:
Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die.
As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated.
Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death.
Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales.
Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the creative heart of Hebden Bridge – a former mill town famed for its independent spirit and as a filming location for the BBC TV series Happy Valley.
Today’s competitors are friends Emma and Sophie, who first met on a fashion shoot for Dove House Hospice. Now they’re going head-to-head to raise as much money as possible for the charity that brought them together. Guiding them are expert vintage thrifters – and husbands – Tom and Terry.
The teams quickly reveal very different shopping styles. Sophie and Tom dive straight into the nearest shop, where Sophie’s love of oversized menswear leads her to a vintage St Michael jacket – a nostalgic find with added appeal thanks to its 'Made in the UK' label. Emma and Terry take a steadier approach, carefully assessing a rare red rotary dial telephone before building a collection packed with retro charm.
The hunt for Joanna’s pick of the day – an original 1970s Holly Hobbie doll – adds extra jeopardy. While Tom hesitates over the gamble, Sophie trusts her instinct and pushes to secure the collectable toy. As time slips away, Emma and Terry uncover a colourful 1960s picnic set and an eye-catching Murano-style glass duck that divides opinion but promises personality at auction.
For the upcycling challenge, creativity takes centre stage. Emma selects a vintage rocking chair and plans to re-cover it using fabric from animal-illustrated curtains – a bold, characterful refresh. Sophie, however, leaves her upcycle decision perilously late, eventually opting for an unexpected sleeping bag with plans to transform it into a statement padded coat.
The final minutes are frantic for Sophie and Tom, who scramble to spend the remainder of their budget. With Joanna urging them on, they squeeze in a last-second dash for additional vintage finds before they run out of time.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must swap browsing rails for the rostrum. Emma channels calm confidence, while Sophie leans into theatrical flair. With bids climbing and pride on the line, it’s a spirited showdown, but whatever the outcome, Dove House Hospice stands to benefit from a creative, chaotic and thoroughly entertaining day on Hebden Bridge's high street.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc:
Chris and Lee travel to Eton Wick to help Andrew and Angela revive their Victorian cottage garden. Once lovingly maintained, it has now fallen into neglect, with a rotten pergola, a decaying arbour seat and overgrown borders in need of care. The uneven, rough surface also makes the garden unsafe and inaccessible for their young son William.
Andrew and Angela dream of putting their own twist on a traditional Victorian cottage garden with timeless tranquillity and modern functionality. They want to create a beautiful, low-maintenance space that’s also accessible for William, who relies on outdoor time because of his disabilities. The garden will feature smooth, accessible pathways, strategic seating areas and a calming, interactive play zone designed with William’s mobility in mind. A secluded corner filled with soothing plants and comfortable seating will offer the family a place to unwind and reconnect after hospital visits and busy days.
Andrew and Angela met while on holiday in Dublin and have shared a love of travel ever since. Angela, originally from America, and Andrew, a seasoned world traveller himself, settled down when she became pregnant, buying their home to start a family. But life soon took an unexpected turn when their son William was born prematurely with a rare condition, bilateral tibial hemimelia, causing severe malformations in both legs and feet. Their renovation plans were put on hold as hospital visits, surgeries and recoveries became part of everyday life. Earlier this year, William underwent an amputation of his right leg and is now learning to walk confidently with his prosthetic. Three further surgeries on his left leg are planned, with more likely into his early twenties.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Rose Ayling-Ellis came to fame on EastEnders and captured the nation’s hearts when she won Strictly. Since then, she’s used her platform to campaign for deaf rights. Now, Rose goes in search of her family history. She’s heard a rumour of Italian ancestry on her father’s side and is hoping for a bit of drama on her mum’s.
Rose starts by visiting her mum in Kent. Rose’s mum has an intriguing picture of Rose’s three-time great-grandmother. The family story is that she ran a pub in Birmingham with an iron fist. But Rose’s mum doesn’t know her name or if any of the stories are true. To find out, Rose heads to Birmingham.
Local historian Simon Briercliffe helps Rose put a name to her three-time great-grandmother – Agnes Chilton. Trade directories and census returns show that Agnes and her husband Alfred ran a pub. A local newspaper article tells a story worthy of an EastEnders plotline: Agnes and Alfred were caught up in an altercation with a customer, resulting in a court appearance. Rose discovers that Alfred died aged 48, leaving Agnes a widow. Fearing the worst for a woman on her own at that time, Rose is happy to discover that shortly after Alfred’s death Agnes moved to her own pub, the Aston Tavern.
Rose heads there to meet historian Professor Julie-Marie Strange and discovers that Agnes married again at the age of 50. However, two years later, Agnes’s second husband also died. Once again, Agnes was undeterred and expanded the pub further. Rose is delighted to find out that the current landlord of the Aston Tavern has named the rooms after former landlords, including Agnes. As Rose goes to find the room named after her ancestor, she reflects on what a resilient woman Agnes was.
Rose then turns to the paternal side of the family. At her dad’s house in Somerset, Rose’s grandma tells her that her father, Rose’s great-grandad, came from a huge family of 17 children. She doesn’t know a lot about them but remembers that her grandfather, James Welland, Rose’s great-great-grandad, lost his hand in an accident, and she also recalls her dad telling her that when he was a child, they were very poor and lived in a squat in Exeter. Rose also asks about the Italian connection. Rose’s dad explains that this story came through his dad’s side of the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads west to the seaside town of Aberystwyth, famous for its Victorian pier and unpredictable weather. Battling the rain are mother-and-son duo Margaret and Endaf, both hoping their shared love of a bargain will translate into serious profit for charity.
With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they’re paired with expert thrifters and sent racing around Aberystwyth’s charity shops. Endaf starts strongly, snapping up a quality blazer for under a tenner before confidently adding crystal glasses and rare Babycham glasses to his haul. He later spots a vintage wool-and-cashmere jacket, Joanna’s pick of the day, and takes a chance on a violin, proving he is willing to think outside the box.
Margaret, meanwhile, wastes no time securing her upcycle item – a nest of dark wood tables bought for just £3. She also picks up Dutch wooden clogs, a vintage leather messenger bag and gambles on an expensive suede jacket, carefully selecting items she believes have strong resale appeal. The contest has a warm but competitive family dynamic, with playful rivalry building between mum and son as the clock ticks down.
At the transformation stage, Endaf’s plain 80s leather jacket is dramatically reworked with fabric paint and new gold hardware by upcycle entrepreneur Emma Deeks, turning it into a bold statement piece. Margaret’s modest £3 tables are transformed by using a poured-paint technique, creating a colourful, marbled finish that completely reinvents them.
Then comes the live-streamed auction. Endaf grows in confidence as he pitches his items, using detail and humour to drive bids higher, especially on the vintage Burton jacket and his upcycled leather piece. Margaret charms viewers with her warmth and storytelling, successfully selling her clogs and making a strong profit on her upcycled tables.
When the totals are combined with their online sales, who will win between mother and son? The real triumph is for their chosen charity, the British Heart Foundation, with an impressive amount raised in total.
Rain-soaked, good-humoured and full of personality, this contest is a heartwarming family face-off that proves thrifting talent might just run in the family.

programme.title: Alleluia
programme.desc:
Bidh Iain MacFhionghain a' toirt thugainn measgachadh de laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean. Anns a’ phrògram-sa, bidh Iain a’ leughadh bhon leabhar Gliocas bhon Bhìoball le Dòmhnall Saunders agus cluinnidh sibh rannan bho Leabhar Cheist Na Màthar le Màiri NicAonghais Cuideachd cluinnear laoidhean freagarrach, feadhainn air an clàradh as ùr airson Alleluia. Am measg nan seinneadairean bidh Marcas Mac an Tuairneir, Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Chloe Steele.
Cuideachd òran co-aimsireil bho Mhàiri Callan a seinn Togaibh na Drochaidean mu dheidhinn dòchas agus dàimh. Agus cluinnidh sibh Sian a’ seinn na h-aonaibh sailm thairis air an tri fichead. An t-seachdain-sa bheir Jenna Chuimeanach dhuinn leughadh agus smuain.
Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings. Iain reads excerpts from Gliocas bhon Bhìoball by Donald Saunders, and Mairi MacInnes narrates from The Mother’s Catechism.
Iain also introduces fitting hymns and psalms, some recorded especially for this series. Mary Ann Kennedy, Marcas Mac an Tuairneir and Chloe Steele are among the singers.
Màiri Callan sings the contemporary arrangement, Togaibh na Drochaidean, a song of affinity and hope. Sian perform Psalm 61 from the extensive Alleluia archive and Jenna Cumming presents her chosen reading and reflects on its personal meaning.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Iain Mackinnon.

programme.title: Ruairidh Gray aig Barrowland
programme.desc:
Megan NicGill-Fhaolain le cuirm bhon t-seinneadair Gàidhlig, Ruairidh Gray, sa Bharrowland Ballroom. Bho bhith a’ cluich ann an tallaichean-baile an Uibhist a Deas agus a’ coisinn dà bhonn òr aig a’ Mhòd, a’ cluich cuide ris san talla-ciùil as cliùitiche ann an Alba, tha cluicheadairean ceòl-dannsa, le ‘dachaigh rock & roll’ ga thionndaidh gu bhith na àite coinneachaidh do na Gàidheil. Megan MacLellan presents a concert from Gaelic singer Ruairidh Gray at the Barrowland Ballroom. Starting out in small village halls in South Uist, The Mòd double gold medalist is now joined onstage in Scotland’s most iconic music venue by a stellar cast of dance band musicians.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc:
Tha Kate Nicleòid, maighdeann-mhara Innse Gall, gar toirt air turas gu cuid de na ceàrnaidhean àlainn nach eil cho aithnichte sna h-Eileanan an Iar agus bidh i a’ coinneachadh ri seanchaidhean le sgeulachdan iongantach mu na h-àiteachan air a bheil i gu math dèidheil, os cionn agus fon uisge.
Anns an treas prògram, tha Kate agus a h-athair a’ cumail orra gu Pabaigh, Easaigh agus Ceann a Deas na Hearadh, far am iad a’ gabhail cuairt timcheall nan eileanan àlainn seo fon mhuir agus tioram air tìr. Tha Kate a’ faighinn facal air Fiona NicChoinnich ann an Strannda gus ionnsachadh mu dheidhinn nam peathraichean Pàislig agus mar a bha iadsan an urra ris a’ chiad phìos de chlò Hearach a chaidh a reic, a tha a-nis aithnichte air feadh an t-saoghail, agus bidh i a’ tachairt ri Coinneach Caimbeul aig a bheil dlùth cheangal ri Eilean Phabaigh.
Bidh i cuideachd a’ coinneachadh ris an tuilleadh ròin agus a’ toirt sùil air bòidhchead nan coilltean feamainn iongantach rin lorg fon uisge ann an Easaigh.
Kate Macleod, The Hebridean Mermaid, takes us on a journey to some of the hidden gems of the Hebrides, meeting tradition bearers with remarkable stories about the places she loves to visit the most, above and below the water.
Kate and her dad journey to Pabbay, Ensay and the South of Harris, where they explore these beautiful islands underwater and on dry land.
She meets Fiona MacKenzie in the village of Strond to learn about how the Paisley Sisters were responsible for the first ever commercially produced web of the world-renowned Harris Tweed, and she talks to Kenneth Campbell who has a strong connection to the Island of Pabbay. Kate continues attempting to befriend seals and takes in the beauty of Ensay's underwater seaweed forests.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Kate Macleod Executive Producer - Margaret Mary Murray Producer - Peter Macqueen Production Manager - Marion Maclean.

programme.title: Plaigh air Bord
programme.desc:
Seventy years ago in 1952, British scientists moored a floating laboratory off Tolsta on the Isle of Lewis to animal test the efficiency of viruses, including bubonic plague, as biological weapons.
Bubonic plague once killed half the population of Europe, so the government was appalled when a fishing boat with a crew of 18 sailed through a cloud of virus. The programme reveals how the experiments were hushed up and the fishermen never told of their exposure to the plague.
Deich bliadhna fichead air ais (1952) bha air acair far chladaichean Tholstaidh ann an Leòdhas, bàta coltach ri laboratoraidh le luchd saidheans Breatannach a’ dèanamh dheuchainnean air beathaichean feuch dè cho èifeachdach ‘s a bhiodh bhìoraisean, a’phlàigh dhubh nam measg, mar armachd bìth-eolasach. Aig aon àm mharbhar dàrna leth sluaigh na Roinn Eòrpa leis a’ phlàigh dhubh, chan iongnadh e gun robh an riaghaltas air an uabhasachadh gun do sheòl bàta le ochd duine deug de chriutha tro sgòth de bhìoras. Tha am prògram ag innse mar a chumar na deuchainnean fo chleòca agus mar nach do dh’innsear riamh do na h-iasgairean gun deach iad tro sgòth luma làn plàigh.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Cathy MacDonald Director - Les Wilson.

programme.title: Na Lorgairean Aillse/The Cancer Detectives
programme.desc:
Tha an sgeulachd mu mar a thàinig deuchainn-sàbhalach airson aillse mhuineal na machlaig gu beatha bhoireannaich àbhaisteach cho annasach ’s a tha e cho iongantach ris a’ bhuidheann de dhaoine a chruthaich e: in-imreach Grèigeach, an Dtr. George Papanicolaou; a bhean dhàna, Mary; neach-ealain Iapanach, Hashime Murayama; an Dtr. Helen Dickens, lèigh-eòlaiche bhan Aifrigeanach Ameireacanach ann am Philadelphia; agus clas gu tur ùr de luchd-saidheans bhoireann, aithnichte mar eòlaichean-cheallan.
Cha robh san deuchainn ach toiseach-tòiseachaidh. Aon uair ’s gun deach a dhearbhadh cho èifeachdach ’s a bha i, dh’fheumadh an iomairt gus an deuchainn-smiùraidh a thoirt gu nam milleanan de bhoireannaich gluasad nàiseanta a thogail air feadh Ameireagaidh. Tha Na Lorgairean Aillse ag innse sgeulachd nach deach a h-innse roimhe, mun chiad chogadh riamh an aghaidh aillse, agus na daoine a rinn strì gun stad gus boireannaich a shàbhaladh bhon phrìomh aillse a bha uair gam marbhadh.
The story of how the life-saving cervical cancer test became an ordinary part of women’s lives is as unusual and remarkable as the coalition of people who ultimately made it possible: a Greek immigrant, Dr George Papanicolaou; his intrepid wife, Mary; Japanese-born artist, Hashime Murayama; Dr Helen Dickens, an African American OB/GYN in Philadelphia; and an entirely new class of female scientists known as cyto-screeners.
But the test was just the beginning. Once it proved effective, the campaign to make Pap smears available to millions of women required nothing short of a national mobilisation across America. The programme tells the untold story of the first-ever war on cancer, and the people who fought tirelessly to save the population from what had been the number one cancer killer of women.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc:
Skipinnish le Coire Bhreacan ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann.
Skipinnish perform Coire Bhreacan in front of thousands of fans at a concert celebrating 25 years of the band, from Edinburgh Castle.

programme.title: Trail West aig Barrowland
programme.desc:
Cuirm shònraichte a’ comharrachadh 15 bliadhna de Trail West. Bho thallaichean-baile is taighean-seinnse air feadh na Gàidhealtachd ’s nan Eilean gu na h-ionadan-ciùil as motha an Alba, tha an còmhlan a’ cur a’ chuirm as motha aca air dòigh sa Bharrowland Ballroom, len luchd-leantainn ann an Glaschu airson pàrtaidh mòr a’ Chost’ an Iar. Le agallamhan leis a’ chòmhlan agus criomagan bhon chuirm. A special concert to celebrate 15 years of Trail West, who have gone from performing in village halls and pub gigs across the Highlands and Islands to Scotland’s biggest venues. The Tiree band put on their mightiest show to date at the iconic Barrowland Ballroom as fans descend on Glasgow for a massive west coast party. Featuring interviews with band members plus concert highlights.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.desc:
Tha dòighean-fuirich Sgioba nan Luch dèanamh dragh do Mhossy 's e cur roimhe fuireach leis fhèin son greis. Ge-tà, gun cuideachadh on sgioba, chan eil Mossy cho comasach coimhead às a dhèidh fhèin!
The living habits of the Shrew Crew have started to annoy Mossy, leading him to believe it would be best to live alone for a while. However, without the help of the crew, Mossy isn't quite as competent as he thought. The puffin burrow has been flooded and May invites the little pufflings to come and stay with her until the mess is fixed. Although there's excitement and merriment at first, Baba soon becomes unsure about sleeping so far from home. programme.title: Golf: Mun Cuairt Alba
programme.desc:
Le còrr air 550 raon-goilf tha Alba cliùiteach mar dhachaigh ghoilf. Tha an sreath 6-pàirt seo a’ gabhail turas air feadh na dùthcha gu na cùrsaichean ainmeil agus na seudan àlainn nach eil cho iomraiteach, a’ fosgladh ar sùilean gu goilf. Cluinnidh sinn bho ghoilfearan sean is òg, fireann is boireann, goilfearan dall is goilfearan ciorramach, agus bho chuid a bhios a' cosnadh beòshlaint à goilf.
An t-seachdain-sa, gabhaidh sinn sgrìob-adhair mu chuairt raointean-goilf ann an Siorrachd Àir, nam measg Prestwick far an robh a’ chiad Open ann an 1860. Tha am Pro Kieron Stevenson a’ cluiche am ‘Postage Stamp’ 8mh toll aig Royal Troon, agus tha coidse proifeiseanta Keil Beveridge a’ toirt seachad comhairle na seachdaine airson dòigh-cluiche.
Scotland has over 550 golf courses and is regarded worldwide as the home of golf. This series takes us on a journey around the country to explore some of the well-known courses as well as some of its hidden gems, and opens the door to golf. We hear from golfers young and old, male and female, blind golfers and disabled golfers, and from those who make their living working in golf, plus we capture a few tips from the professionals along the way.
In this episode, we take an aerial journey along the Ayrshire coast and learn about the first Open Championship which took place at Prestwick. Pro Kieron Stevenson shows us how to play the signature 'Postage Stamp' 8th hole at Royal Troon, and professional coach Keil Beveridge demonstrates his weekly top playing tip.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Expert - Keil Beveridge Producer - Patricia Macleod Director - Scott Brown Editor - Jonny Craigmile.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Tha Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na ciad ceumannan a tha a dhìth airson ar misneachadh gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Thairis air an t-sreath, bidh i a’ dèiligeadh ri facail is abairtean air measgachadh de chuspairean co-cheangailte ri gach taobh de ar beatha. Leis gun do dh’ionnsaich i fhèin, bheir Joy dhuinn briathrachas mu charaidean, an dachaigh, an teaghlach, obair agus an aimsir am measg gu leòr eile ann an dòigh a tha sìmplidh agus furasta a thuigsinn. Bidh stiùireadh ann cuideachd a thaobh a bhith a’ cleachdadh abairtean, le eisimpleirean soilleir ann an dramathan goirid.
Coinnichidh sinn luchd-ionnsachaidh èasgaidh, feadhainn a tha ag ionnsachadh as ùr agus cuid a bha fileanta agus a sguir ga cleachdadh, agus iadsan a th’ air a bhith ag ionnsachadh fad bhliadhnaichean. Agus bidh Calum MacIlleathain a’ toirt sealladh eile dhuinn air Alba is e ann an diofar àitichean air feadh na dùthcha.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne: www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan a tha ri fhaighinn air BBC Sounds.
Joy Dunlop guides viewers through the first steps to inspire us to speak Gaelic. Throughout the series, she introduces words and phrases on a variety of everyday topics. A Gaelic learner herself, Joy supports us through pronunciation and vocabulary on topics such as friends, family, home, work and weather.
We meet diligent learners who have embraced speaking Gaelic, from new learners to lapsed native speakers and the on-off learners who have improved their language skills over the decades. And the intrepid Calum Maclean takes us on adventures to hidden treasures around Scotland.
Supporting materials can be found online: www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Presenter - Calum Maclean Producer - Colin MacLeod Executive Producer - Una McDonald.

programme.desc:

Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail
programme.desc:
Tha Linda NicLeòid agus Hannah McKirdy a’ toirt thugaibh a’ chlann a bhuannaich farpaisean aig a’ Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail ann an Glaschu. Seo a’ chiad latha de dh’ fharpaisean aig Mòd na cloinne agus tha a’ phrosbaig air luchd-ionnsachaidh. Bidh duaisean rin glèidheadh airson seinn aon-neach, seinn chòisirean, aithris bàrdachd agus aithris sgeulachdan agus nam measg bidh Bonn Cuimhneachan Sheumais C Mhic a’ Phi airson seinn aon-neach nigheannan aois 13-15 – aon de phrìomh dhuaisean an latha. Cluinnear cuideachd cuid den òigridh a shoirbhich anns na farpaisean ciùil Disathuirne. Tha clann bho air feadh Alba a’ gabhail pàirt anns a’ Mhod agus bidh cuid dhen fheadhainn a bhuannaich gan clàradh ann an stiùidio a’ BhBC ann an Talla Chonsairt Rìoghail Ghlaschu.
Linda MacLeod and Hannah McKirdy present the winning competitors from the Royal National Mòd in Glasgow. This is the first day of the children’s competitions and the focus is primarily on Gaelic learners. Prizes for solo singing, choral singing, poetry recitation and storytelling are up for grabs, including the coveted James C MacPhee Memorial Medal for girls 13-15 for solo singing.
The programme also features some winners of the junior instrumental competitions on Saturday. Competitors from schools all over Scotland took part and winning performances were filmed in the BBC’s studio at Glasgow Royal Concert Hall.

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions
programme.desc:
Julie Fowlis agus Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh le taghadh ciùil bho dhà dheichead den phrògram ciùil cliùiteach, ‘Transatlantic Sessions’ ann an cuideachd sàr luchd-ciùil thraidiseanta is dhùthchasach à Alba, Eirinn agus Na SA. Anns a’ phrògram seo, cothrom air measgachadh de stoidhlean ciùil ann an taisbeanaidhean ‘Sessions’ le Eddi Reader, Karan Casey, Cara Dillon, Bruce Molsky agus Ricky Skaggs.
Julie Fowlis and Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh present highlights from two decades of the legendary music show, ‘Transatlantic Sessions’ featuring some of the biggest trad and roots music stars from Scotland, Ireland and the US. In this programme, fans of the 'Sessions' can see a variety of musical styles with performances from Eddi Reader, Karan Casey, Cara Dillon, Bruce Molsky and Ricky Skaggs. Presenter - Julie Fowlis Presenter - Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh Executive Producer - Alasdair MacCuish Director - Iain Macleod Producer - Ewan Duncan Production Manager - Gillian MacLean.

programme.title: Fergie, The Ceilidh King
programme.desc:
Program a tha a’ dèanamh luaidh air am fear-ciùil Fergie Dòmhnallach à Loch Abar a chaochail na bu thràithe am-bliadhna. Lìon e tallaichean-baile air feadh Alba le daoine ga ghabhail fhèin agus a stoidhle ciùil rin cridheachan. Agus ge bith càit am biodh Fergie, bhiodh seanchas agus craic am pailteas! Bha tuigse air leth aige air a’ cheangal a bha eadar daoine agus ceòl agus, leis an tuigse sin agus a sgil fhèin, bha na puirt aige tarraingeach do dh’iomadh ginealach airson 60 bliadhna. B’ e an Ceilidh King, fear-ciùil air an robh meas aig daoine fad is farsaing agus gheibh sinn sealladh air an duine fhèin bho theaghlach, a charaidean agus bho luchd-ciùil eile a bha eòlach air.
A tribute to Lochaber musician Fergie MacDonald who died in 2024. Fergie filled halls and captured hearts across Scotland with his distinctive West Coast musical style, as well as his infectious sense of humour. With a unique understanding of how people connect with music, he sustained a 60-year career and his popularity spanned generations. We hear from musicians, friends and family about what made the Ceilidh King one of Scotland’s most loved musicians.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Producer - Annie Cheape Executive Producer - Maureen MacLeod Executive Producer - Margaret Mary Murray Editor - Chris Gillies.

Air a sgrìobhadh agus a chluich le talant sonraichte, ùr agus steidhichte. Le Artair Donald, Ellen NicDhòmhnaill, Darren Mac’illEathain, Carina MacLeod, Hannah McKirdy, Lana Pheutan agus Daibhidh Walker. A gabhail a-steach duiligheadasan oifis na báta-aiseig, gniomhan grain an aghaidh bos na h-obrach, agus tairgsean-pòsaidh gu buan.

Includes problems at the ferry office, an all-action grudge against the boss in the workplace and an everlasting proposal.

programme.desc:

programme.title: Turas a Bhradain
programme.desc: Iasgach a' bhradain air cuid de na h-aibhnichean is àlluinne an Alba - cuide ri Neen NicAoidh. An odyssey through Scotland's fishing rivers with Neen MacKay. Presenter - Neen MacKay.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc:
Joy Dunlop gar toirt tro na h-ath cheumannan gus Gàidhlig a bhruidhinn. Tha Liam Alastair Crouse às Na Stàitean Aonaichte a’ tadhal air Joy san stiùidio agus tha Calum MacIlleathain a’ gabhail turas bàta gus lorg fhaighinn air eòin-mhara gu math sònraichte.
Lorgar tuilleadh stuthan taic air-loidhne aig www.speakgaelic.scot agus ann an sreath phodcastan air BBC Sounds.
Joy Dunlop guides us through the next steps to speak Gaelic. Liam Alastair Crouse from the United States chats to Joy in the studio and Calum Maclean takes a boat trip to a colony of characterful seabirds.
Supporting materials can be found online at www.speakgaelic.scot and in the SpeakGaelic podcasts on BBC Sounds. Presenter - Joy Dunlop Executive Producer - Una McDonald.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc:
Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA.
Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail
programme.desc:
Tha Linda NicLeòid agus Hannah McKirdy a’ toirt thugaibh cuid dhen òigridh a shoirbhich air an dàrna latha de Mhòd na cloinne ann an Glaschu. Seo an latha far a bheil clann fhileanta bho air feadh na dùthcha a’ taisbeanadh nan tàlantan aca. Anns a’ phrògram seo, chì sibh farpaisich a ghlèidh na bràistean, na cuachan is na gill-dhùbhlain airson aithris bàrdachd, seinn chòisirean, seinn aon-neach agus seinn-càraid. Nam measg, an nighean ’s an gille a thog na prìomh dhuaisean airson seinn san t-seann nòs.
Linda MacLeod and Hannah McKirdy are in Glasgow’s Royal Concert Hall to present winners from the second day of coverage of the children’s Mòd in Glasgow. The spotlight falls on young fluent Gaelic speakers.
The programme features winners who will take home a range of gold badges, cups and trophies for various competitions - including solo singing, choral singing and poetry recitation. Plus, winners of the premier prizes for traditional singing.

programme.title: Miann na Maighdinn-mara/Mermaid Tales
programme.desc:
Tha Kate Nicleòid, maighdeann-mhara Innse Gall, gar toirt air turas gu cuid de na ceàrnaidhean àlainn nach eil cho aithnichte sna h-Eileanan an Iar agus bidh i a’ coinneachadh ri seanchaidhean le sgeulachdan iongantach mu na h-àiteachan air a bheil i gu math dèidheil, os cionn agus fon uisge.
Anns a’ cheathramh prògram, tha Kate a’ dèanamh air Beàrnaraigh na Hearadh agus a’ tachairt ri muinntir an àite, nam measg, Dòmhnall MacIllEathain a tha ag innse dhi mu dhòigh-beatha an àite sna làithean a dh’fhalbh, agus mu dheidhinn am fuamhaire ainmeil, Aonghas Mòr MacAsgaill, a rinn beòshlaint le cho àrd ’s a bha e – seachd troighean ’s naoi òirleach!
Tha i a’ cluinntinn sgeulachdan mu bheatha Ruairidh Sheathaich agus e na bhalach òg a’ fàs suas ann am Beàrnaraigh ’s a’ dol do dh’ àrd-sgoil sna Hearadh, am measg seanchas inntinneach mu chruth-tìre an eilein.
Tha i cuideachd a’ dèanamh oidhirp snàmh cuide ri na ròin agus bidh i ann an caidheag air a’ mhuir mu thimcheall An Tràigh Iar – an tràigh eireachdail a chaidh ainmeachadh bho chionn ghoirid mar an tràigh as bòidhche anns an Roinn Eòrpa.
Kate Macleod, The Hebridean Mermaid, takes us on a journey to some of the hidden gems of the Hebrides, meeting tradition bearers with remarkable stories about the places she loves to visit the most, above and below the water.
Kate makes her way to Berneray and meets locals such as Donald MacLean, who explains what life was like there in days gone by. He shares the story of Angus MacAskill, who made a living from his giant height - all seven foot, nine inches of him!
Roddy Shaw shares his story of growing up on Berneray and attending high school in Harris, as well as some interesting folklore about the landscape of the island. Kate attempts to swim with seals and also kayaks around the shores of the stunning West Beach, which was recently named the most beautiful beach in Europe.
In Gaelic with English subtitles Presenter - Kate Macleod Executive Producer - Margaret Mary Murray Production Manager - Marion Maclean Producer - Peter Macqueen.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap set on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Abigail
programme.desc:
Bàlaichean Banana, còrdaidh 'ad ris a' mhòr-chuid. Tha Abigail gan dèanamh às ùr, 's gan taisbeanadh gu brèagha. Greim-bìdh glè bhlasta.
Banana Balls, most people will love them. Abigail makes them from scratch and presents them beautifully. A very tasty snack.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Abigail Maciver Producer - Kenneth Stewart Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Executive Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay.

programme.title: Alleluia
programme.desc:
Bidh Iain MacFhionghain a' toirt thugainn measgachadh de laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean. Anns a’ phrògram-sa, bidh Iain a’ leughadh bhon leabhar Gliocas bhon Bhìoball le Dòmhnall Saunders agus cluinnidh sibh rannan bho Leabhar Cheist Na Màthar le Màiri NicAonghais Cuideachd cluinnear laoidhean freagarrach, feadhainn air an clàradh as ùr airson Alleluia. Am measg nan seinneadairean bidh Marcas Mac an Tuairneir, Màiri Anna NicUalraig agus Chloe Steele.
Cuideachd òran co-aimsireil bho Mhàiri Callan a seinn Togaibh na Drochaidean mu dheidhinn dòchas agus dàimh. Agus cluinnidh sibh Sian a’ seinn na h-aonaibh sailm thairis air an tri fichead. An t-seachdain-sa bheir Jenna Chuimeanach dhuinn leughadh agus smuain.
Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings. Iain reads excerpts from Gliocas bhon Bhìoball by Donald Saunders, and Mairi MacInnes narrates from The Mother’s Catechism.
Iain also introduces fitting hymns and psalms, some recorded especially for this series. Mary Ann Kennedy, Marcas Mac an Tuairneir and Chloe Steele are among the singers.
Màiri Callan sings the contemporary arrangement, Togaibh na Drochaidean, a song of affinity and hope. Sian perform Psalm 61 from the extensive Alleluia archive and Jenna Cumming presents her chosen reading and reflects on its personal meaning.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Iain Mackinnon.

programme.title: Dan & Gran
programme.sub-title: Bananathan aig Beul an Là ║ S1E13/52
programme.desc:
Grumblestunk is sure she saw an enormous banana when she walked Stink on the beach early that morning. Stan and Gran spy a mystery - but no banana!
Tha Greannarlobht deimhinnt' gum fac' i banana mòr uabhasach nuair a bha i a' coiseachd le Samh air an tràigh, tràth air a' mhadainn ud, is tha Dan is Gran a' faicinn rùn-dìomhair... ach 'n eil sgeul air banana! Dan - Ellen Macdonald Gran - Kathleen MacInnes Seanair - Tom MacIver Greannarlobht - Maureen MacLeod Producer - Kenneth Stewart Production Manager - Mairi Macleod Executive Producer - Rachel Ellen Mackay.

programme.title: Losgannan
Froglets
programme.sub-title: Sgitheadh ║ Losgannan. S1E20/26. Skiing ║ Losgannan. S1E20/26
programme.desc:
Air sgìthean is bùird-shneachda, thèid na Losgannan aig astar air beanntan chuibhrigean.
The Froglets don home-made skis and snowboards, in order to whizz down a mountain of winter duvets.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc:
Nuair tha Beag Chlangair ’g iasgach san long-chiùil, tha e a’ glacadh rudeigin iongantach. Tha e coltach ri bàla meatailt. Ach dè th’ ann?
When Beag Chlangair is out fishing in the music boat, he catches something amazing. It looks like a metal ball, but what is it? Narrator - Iain Mackinnon Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc:
Tha Meanbh Chlangair a’ cluich ceòl àlainn le a caraidean lusach. Tha Mamaidh den bheachd gu bheil Meanbh cho tàlantach ach, nuair a tha Meanbh ’g iarraidh air Mamaidh seinn còmhla riutha, chan eil i idir deònach sin a dhèanamh. Carson nach seinn i?
Meanbh Chlangair plays lovely music with her flower friends. Mamaidh thinks that Meanbh is so talented but, when Meanbh asks Mamaidh to sing with them, she refuses. Why does she not want to sing? Narrator - Iain Mackinnon Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Peicein/Petit
programme.sub-title: Chan eil mi ag iarraidh piuthar tuilleadh!/I want to be an only child again ║ Peicein/PetitS1E10/26
programme.desc:
Tha Peicein sgìth dhe phiuthar bheag agus tha e a’ co-dhùnadh nach eil e ag iarraidh piuthar tuilleadh. Às dèidh feuchainn ri dhol air ais ann an ùine airson Tìona a thilleadh dhan bhùth agus pàrantan ùr fhaighinn, tha e ag ionnsachadh gum feum e daoine a leanas òrdain, ma tha e airson a bhith na rìgh.
Petit is tired of his little sister and decides that he will be an only child again. After trying to go back in time, give back Tina for store credit and switching parents, he discovers that to be king, he needs people to reign over. Various - Linda MacLeod Various - Kim Carnie Various - Calum MacDonald Various - Calum MacAmhlaigh Various - Eoghan MacDonald Producer - Linda MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill MacLeod Editor - Chas Chalmers Production Company - Solus Productions.

programme.title: ’S E Iasg a Th’Annam (I’m a Fish)
programme.desc:
Tha Crosgag ag innse dhuinn mar ’s urrainn dhaibh seasamh, gluasad agus ith’ - ged nach eil cnàmhan annta.
The starfish tells us how they can stand, walk and eat even though they don’t have any bones to hold them up. Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Ishbel Maclean.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc:
Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Mischa Nic a’ Phearsain a’ leughadh Mòd Mheadhan-oidhche. Chaidh an stòiridh a sgrìobhadh le Mòrag NicNèill agus a dhealbhachadh le Kasia Matyjaszek.
A bedtime story for young children. Mischa MacPherson reads Mòd Mheadhan-oidhche, written by Morag MacNeil and illustrated by Kasia Matyjaszek. Presenter - Mischa Macpherson.

programme.title: Clo Beag Chirsty Bella
programme.desc:
Tha Chirsty Bella ag iarraidh Clò Hearach a dhèanamh…tha e gu math nas fhasa smaoineachadh air sin na tha e ga chuir an gnìomh. Tha ì a’ fuireach ann an Scalpaigh, Na Hearadh. Tha gaol aice air a h-eilean agus tha ì ga cumail fhèin trang le bhith a reic uighean agus a dèanamh dannsa Gàidheallach. ‘S toigh leatha cuideachd an clò ainmeil clùiteach: Clò Hearach. Tha an t-seann bheairt mar time machine, ga toirt air ais gu lìnn an fhearsaid, nan càrd, ‘s a spàl. An teid orra à clò a dhèanamh ann an àm?
Chirsty Bella wants to produce her own Harris tweed but that is easier said than done. She lives in Scalpay, a little village in the Isle of Harris, loves her island and keeps herself going through little jobs like selling eggs and traditional Scottish Highland dancing. She also loves the famous and traditional fabric: Harris Tweed. The original Harris Tweed loom is like a time machine that takes her back over a hundred years to the age of spindles, combs and shuttles. Will she manage to weave her cloth in time?

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.sub-title: An Dachaigh: Miann mo Chridhe ║ S1E27/52
programme.desc:
Nuair a tha Belle leòinte is air chall, tha Sebastian ga lorg. Càite bheil i? Chan eil fiù 's fios aig Anton, am poidsear, càil mu dhèidhinn. Ach, an uair sin, tha Sebastian a' cluinntinn mun Fhasgadh Shona.
When Belle is injured and lost, Sebastian goes searching for her - where is she? Even Anton the poacher doesn’t know anything about it. However, Sebastian then hears about the Happy Shelter. Sebastian - Ellen Macdonald Adele - Mischa Macpherson Gabriel - Iona Davidson Casper - Calum MacKinnon Angelina - Emily Davidson Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Seonaidh
Shaun the Sheep
programme.sub-title: Am Meaban ║ Seonaidh. S4E21/30. The Intruder ║ Seonaidh. S4E21/30
programme.desc:
Nuair a thèid iarraidh air Bitzer cuidhteas fhaighinn air starrag chrosta, tha deagh bheachd aig Seonaidh air mar a thèid aca a dhèanamh le bhith a' cleachdadh aodach coimheach. Ach tha am plana a' dol bun os cionn nuair a thèid casaid a chuir air gur e mèirleach craicte nan cearc de Thuathanas Mossybottom.
When the farmer tasks Bitzer with ridding the farm of a pesky crow, Shaun comes up with an ingenious disguise to fool the intruder. However, the plan backfires when he's suspected of being the crazed chicken thief of Mossybottom Farm.

programme.title: Mòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail
programme.desc:

Bekah and Zach from CBBC ALBA, along with The L.A.B. Scotland, visit pupils from Meadowburn Primary School to find out what 40 years of Gaelic Medium Education means to them.

programme.title: Flix
programme.desc:
Tha Flix ‘son film fhaicinn ach, gu mì-fhortanach, the e ro òg ‘son fhaicinn. Dè nì e? Bi faiceallach dè mhiannaicheas tu!
Flix would like to see a film, but unfortunately he’s too young to get in. What will he do now? Be careful what you wish for! Flix - Derek MacIntosh Munchkin - Calum MacKinnon Tabaidh - Claire Frances MacNeil Colza - Mischa Macpherson Zeno - Lana Beaton Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Alec Macdonald.

programme.title: Mòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail
programme.desc:
Tha Cathy NicDhòmhnaill a' toirt thugaibh farpais chriochnachaidh a’ Bhuinn Òir, beò bhon a’ Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail ann an Glaschu.
Às dèidh na ro-fharpaisean na bu tràithe san latha nochdaidh na seinneadairean a shoirbhich air beulaibh na britheamhan ann am prìomh thalla, Talla Chonsairt Rìoghail Ghlaschu, agus iad ag amas air Buinn Òir a’ Chomuinn Ghàidhealaich a ghlèidheadh. Bidh farpaisich na bliadhna-sa an dùil gun tèid aca air a bhith cho soirbheachail sa bha Caitlyn Yule agus Fionnlagh Iain Morse a ghlèidh na Buinn Òir ann an Loch Abar an uiridh.
Bidh dithis eòlaiche còmhla ri Cathy san stiùidio, a’ measadh agus a’ beachdachadh air na seinneadairean. Bidh cothrom ann cuideachd cuid de na farpaisich a shoirbhich nas tràithe air an latha fhaicinn.
Cathy Macdonald presents live coverage of the Gold Medal final for solo singing from the Royal National Mòd in Glasgow.
The leading men and women from the qualifying competitions earlier in the day perform in front of the adjudicators in the Main Auditorium in the Glasgow Royal Concert Hall as they compete for the An Comunn Gàidhealach Gold Medal. This year’s hopefuls will be aiming to emulate the success of Caitlyn Yule and Finlay John Morse in last year’s competition in Lochaber.
Cathy is joined in the studio by two guests with a keen interest in, and knowledge of, Gaelic music and song, to offer assessments of the competitors’ performances. The show also features successful entrants vying for the prestigious Silver Pendant in solo singing for adult learners.

programme.title: Dàna
Scotland's Wild Side
programme.sub-title: Rònaigh ║ Dàna. S2. ALBAE4/6. Rona ║ Dàna. S2. ALBAE4/6
programme.desc:
Largely unexplored by climbers, the island of Rona offers serious adventure potential to those willing to forego comfort and convenience. In order to seek out unclimbed lines and new routes of their own, Coinneach MacFhraing and Owen Sinclair travel to the island and spend a few days wrestling with wet boots, loose rock and the prospect of returning home empty-handed.
Air eilean far nach deach mòran sreap a dhèanamh roimhe, tha Rònaigh a’ tabhann chothroman air leth spòrsail dhan fheadhainn a tha deònach leigeil às de chomhfurtachd is goireasachd.
A’ sireadh slighean ùra dhaibh fhèin nach deach a shreap roimhe, tha Coinneach MacFhraing agus Owen Sinclair a’ siubhal chun an eilean gus latha no dhà a chur seachad a’ dèiligeadh ri bòtannan fliucha, sgrìodan cloiche agus dòchasach nach till iad dhachaigh gun chàil nan cois.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Coinneach MacFhraing Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Director - Hamish MacLeod.

programme.title: Eòin Dino/Dino Birds
programme.desc:
Sùil air mean-fhàs eòin – mar a tha iad air nochdadh ann an iomadach raon agus air atharrachadh gus a bhith beò anns a h-uile àrainneachd air a’ Chruinne-cè. Ach ciamar a ’s urrainn dhuinn am mean-fhàs buadhmhòr seo a mhìneachadh?
Tha eachdraidh nan eun a’ dol air ais 220 millean bliadhna chun a’ chiad dìneasaran, a bha a’ riaghladh airson 150 millean bliadhna agus ’s e na h-eòin an aon sliochd ceangailte riutha – dearbhadh gu bheil dìneasaran fhathast beò nar measg. Chaidh aon de na fosailean as sine de eun ùr a lorg bho chionn ghoirid agus tha sin a’ tabhainn fiosrachadh ùr mu ciamar agus carson gur e iadsan a mhair beò an dèidh astaroid cuir às dhen a’ mhòr chuid de dh’ ainmhidhean a’ chruinne-cè – agus e a’ foillseachadh na tha air cùl soirbheachas a’ mhean-fhàis iongantach aca.
Tha an sreath seo de dhà phrògram a’ leantainn eòlaichean bho air feadh an t-saoghail – ann an Sìona, an Roinn Eòrpa, Aimeireaga agus nas fhaide air falbh – gu làraichean àrc-eòlais agus obair-lannan, is iad a’ sireadh freagairtean.
A fascinating look at the evolution of birds - how they have conquered multiple territories and adapted to every environment on Earth. How can we explain this evolutionary triumph?
The history of birds can be traced back 220 million years to the first dinosaurs, which reigned for 150 million years and of which birds are the only descendants - proof that dinosaurs still live among us. A recent discovery of the oldest fossil of a modern bird offers new clues about how and why they were the only ones to survive the deadly asteroid impact that wiped out most of Earth’s creatures - and reveals the secret of their evolutionary success.
This documentary follows experts from around the world - in China, Europe, America and beyond - to excavation sites and laboratories as they search for answers.
Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Skipinnish Aig A' Chaisteal
programme.desc:
Skipinnish le Coire Bhreacan ann an cuideachd na mìltean de luchd-leantainn aig cuirm-chiùil a’ comharrachadh 25 bliadhna de Skipinnish, bho Chaisteal Dhùn Èideann.
Skipinnish perform Coire Bhreacan in front of thousands of fans at Edinburgh Castle in a concert celebrating 25 years of the band.

programme.title: Ruairidh Gray aig Barrowland
programme.desc:
Megan NicGill-Fhaolain le cuirm bhon t-seinneadair Gàidhlig, Ruairidh Gray, sa Bharrowland Ballroom. Bho bhith a’ cluich ann an tallaichean-baile an Uibhist a Deas agus a’ coisinn dà bhonn òr aig a’ Mhòd, a’ cluich cuide ris san talla-ciùil as cliùitiche ann an Alba, tha cluicheadairean ceòl-dannsa, le ‘dachaigh rock & roll’ ga thionndaidh gu bhith na àite coinneachaidh do na Gàidheil. Megan MacLellan presents a concert from Gaelic singer Ruairidh Gray at the Barrowland Ballroom. Starting out in small village halls in South Uist, The Mòd double gold medallist is now joined onstage in Scotland’s most iconic music venue by a stellar cast of dance band musicians.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Mòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail
programme.desc:
Tha Cathy NicDhòmhnaill a' toirt thugaibh Là Mòr nan Còisirean Dùthchail aig a’ Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail ann an Glaschu. Bidh còisirean bho air feadh Alba a’ strì airson na prìomh dhuaisean - Sgiath Latharna, a bhuannaich Còisir Ghàidhlig Bharraigh ann an 2025 aig Mòd Loch Abar; agus Cuach Cuimhneachan an t-Siorraim MacMhaighstir Caimbeul a ghlèidh Còisir Ghàidhlig Ìle an uiridh.
Còmhla ri Cathy san stiùidio, bidh dithis eòlaiche a’ measadh agus a’ toirt seachad am beachdan air na còisirean bhon dà fharpais iomraiteach seo. Bidh cothrom ann cuideachd èisdeachd ri na buidhnean a choisinn farpaisean còisir a ghabh àite sa mhadainn, nuair a bha Geall-dùbhlain Telebhisean Grampian agus Geall-dùbhlain Cuimhneachan Aline NicCoinnich gan toirt seachad am measg eile.
Cathy Macdonald presents live coverage of the premier competitions for rural choirs at the Royal National Mòd in Glasgow. Choirs from all over Scotland will be competing to win the prestigious Lorn Shield and the Sheriff MacMaster Campbell Memorial Quaich. Barra Gaelic Choir and Islay Gaelic Choir were the respective winners of these two competitions at the Lochaber Mod in 2025.
Cathy will be joined in the studio by two expert guests to offer comment and analysis on the performances in both competitions. The programme will also feature the winning choirs from earlier in the day when the Grampian Television Trophy for Ladies’ Voices and The Aline MacKenzie Memorial Trophy for Puirt à Beul were awarded, amongst others.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc:
Tha Bing agus Sula a’ cur lòn air dòigh còmhla ri Amma. Tha iad a’ nighe churranan, ag ullachadh pheasraichean agus ag ionnsachadh nach eil na h-aon rudan a’ còrdadh ris a h-uile duine.
Bing and Sula prepare lunch together with Amma. They wash carrots and prepare peas and learn that not everybody likes food served the same way. Bing - Benny Walsh Flop - Iain Mackinnon Sula - Holly Duffy Amma - Evelyn Coull MacLeod Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Mairi Morrison.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc:
Nuair a tha Bing agus Flop sa phàirc, tha iad a’ lorg cuilean a tha air chall ris an canar Grianach. Tha Bing agus Grianach ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios iad càirdeil ri chèile agus tha iad a-nis nan caraidean.
When Bing and Flop go to the park, they come across a lost dog whose name is Grianach. Bing takes a shine to Grianach and he decides that she is now his new friend. Bing - Benny Walsh Flop - Iain Mackinnon Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Mairi Morrison.

programme.title: Abadas
programme.desc:
Tha Hari, Ela is Seren air splaoid a' sèideadh bhuilgeanan anns a' ghàradh. Tha tuilleadh sèideadh ri dhèanamh, ge-tà, nuair a tha aon den triùir air an taghadh airson am facal ùr a lorg: trombaid!
Hari, Ela and Seren are having an 'aba-doo-be-dee' time blowing bubbles in the garden. There's more huffing, puffing and blowing to be done when one of the three is chosen to look for today's word; 'trumpet'.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal

Teal and Neep help Abney find something to fill a gap on his shelves. Nothing seems to fit until they find an old radio in the lake, which causes all sorts of excitement! programme.desc:
Tha Crosgag ag innse dhuinn mar ’s urrainn dhaibh seasamh, gluasad agus ith’ - ged nach eil cnàmhan annta.
The starfish tells us how they can stand, walk and eat even though they don’t have any bones to hold them up. Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Editor - Phil Reed Writer - Ishbel Maclean.

programme.title: Peataichean/Pets
programme.desc:
Tha Eilidh NicCarmaig a’ coinneachadh ri clann agus a’ faighinn a-mach mu mar a tha iad a’ coimhead às dèidh agus a’ cluich cuide rim peataichean aig an taigh. Anns a’ phrògram seo, tha Eilidh a’ cèilidh air Callum agus na coin aige Penny is Poppy. ‘S e golden retriever a th’ ann am Poppy agus ‘s e cocker spaniel a th’ ann am Penny agus ‘s e coin àlainn da-rìreabh a th’ annta. Gheibh sinn a-mach barrachd mu bhith a’ coimhead às dèidh coin agus mu na rudan snog is spòrsail a bhios Callum agus na coin aige a’ dèanamh còmhla. Gheibh sinn cuideachd comhairle agus fiosrachadh bho Eilidh fhèin mu bhith a’ làimhseachadh, ag oideachadh agus a’ coimhead às dèidh peataichean.
Eilidh Cormack meets young children who are pet owners. Together, they show, tell and share how they care for, play and interact with their pets at home. In this episode, Eilidh visits Callum and his dogs Penny, a golden retriever, and Poppy, a cocker spaniel. We learn how to look after dogs and find out about all the lovely stuff Callum, Penny and Poppy get up to together. Eilidh also shares fun and interesting facts along with advice on looking after pets at home - including how best to handle, train and feed them. Presenter - Eilidh Cormack Producer - Donna Murchison Production Manager - Mairi MacKinnon.

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc:
Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Dòmhnall Ruadh a’ leughadh Losgann agus Bìobhar. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Simon James agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill.
A bedtime story for young children. Donald Smith reads Losgann agus Bìobhar, written and illustrated by Simon James and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald. Presenter - Donald Smith.

When the Gumbalan mistake Uilidh for the Great Captain Sgrìobair, he enjoys this empowerment very much. However, he has to be cunning when they have troubles with the Bògaisean. programme.sub-title: Am Meaban ║ Seonaidh. S4E21/30. The Intruder ║ Seonaidh. S4E21/30
