Nuair a thèid iarraidh air Bitzer cuidhteas fhaighinn air starrag chrosta, tha deagh bheachd aig Seonaidh air mar a thèid aca a dhèanamh le bhith a' cleachdadh aodach coimheach. Ach tha am plana a' dol bun os cionn nuair a thèid casaid a chuir air gur e mèirleach craicte nan cearc de Thuathanas Mossybottom.
When the farmer tasks Bitzer with ridding the farm of a pesky crow, Shaun comes up with an ingenious disguise to fool the intruder. However, the plan backfires when he's suspected of being the crazed chicken thief of Mossybottom Farm.

Hilda is helpful to a sad and lonely giant, whilst her mum worries about the threats they’ve received and the possible move to a new place - the city of Trolberg. programme.title: Mòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail
programme.desc:
Tha Cathy NicDhòmhnaill a' toirt thugaibh farpais chrìochnachaidh a' Bhuinn Òir airson seinn san t-seann nòs beò bhon a’ Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail ann an Glaschu.
Nochdaidh na seinneadairean a shoirbhich anns na ro-fharpaisean na bu tràithe san latha air beulaibh nam britheamhan ann an Talla Rìoghail Chonsairt Ghlaschu, agus iad ag amas air a’ Bhonn Òir a ghlèidheadh. Bidh dithis eòlaiche còmhla ri Cathy san stiùidio, a’ toirt am beachdan seachad air na farpaisich agus a’ measadh co dh’fhaodadh leantainn ann an ceumannan Màiri Callan agus Donnchadh Macleòid a bhuannaich na buinn anns a’ Ghearasdan an uiridh.
Cuideachd sa phrògram, gheibhear cothrom eile faicinn na còisirean a choisinn na prìomh dhuaisean air là mòr nan còisirean dùthchail na bu tràithe air an latha.
Cathy Macdonald presents live coverage of the Traditional Gold Medal final from this year’s Royal National Mòd in Glasgow.
Having progressed from the qualifying solo singing competitions earlier in the day, the leading men and women perform in front of the adjudicators in the Main Auditorium in Glasgow’s Royal Concert Hall to compete for gold.
Cathy will be joined in the studio by two guests with an in-depth knowledge of Gaelic song. They will offer comment and analysis of the competitors’ performances as entrants aim to emulate Mairi Callan and Duncan Macleod who took home gold in Lochaber in 2025. Plus, another chance to see the winning rural choirs from the two premier competitions held earlier in the day.

programme.title: OMC
programme.desc:
OMC is back! Sketch show featuring a collection of comic characters, spoofs, queue-skipping at the doctors and unexpected puppy love.
Written by and starring the very best in emerging and established comic talent. Featuring Iain Beggs, Darren Maclean, Carina Macleod, Claire Frances MacNeil, Hannah McKirdy, Lana Pheutan and David Walker.
Discover how ceilidh dancing can be a contact sport, a troublesome mermaid shows just why she’s a catch and the latest content from the hottest new influencer Gael Gal.
Tha OMC! air ais le sgeidsichean ùra loma-làn charactaran èibhinn, suidheachaidhean neònach agus ‘spoofs’ gun shamhail.
Bho na sgriobhadairean agus cleasaichean as fheàrr a th’ann seallaidh iad cho cunnartach ’sa dh’fhaodas dannsa bainnse a bhith, tha maighdinn-mhara ag adhbharachadh trioblaid aig muir agus coinnichidh sinn ri ‘influencer’ ùr ann an saoghal na Gàidhlig, Gael Gal.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Various - Lana Pheutan Various - Hannah McKirdy Various - Darren MacLean Various - David Walker Various - Carina MacLeod Various - Iain Beggs Director - Fiann Macleod Producer - Marie McDonald Executive Producer - Rab Christie.

programme.title: Trail West aig Barrowland
programme.desc:
Cuirm shònraichte a’ comharrachadh 15 bliadhna de Trail West. Bho thallaichean-baile is taighean-seinnse air feadh na Gàidhealtachd ’s nan Eilean gu na h-ionadan-ciùil as motha an Alba, tha an còmhlan a’ cur a’ chuirm as motha aca air dòigh sa Bharrowland Ballroom, len luchd-leantainn ann an Glaschu airson pàrtaidh mòr a’ Chost’ an Iar. Le agallamhan leis a’ chòmhlan agus criomagan bhon chuirm. A special concert to celebrate 15 years of Trail West, who have gone from performing in village halls and pub gigs across the Highlands and Islands to Scotland’s biggest venues. The Tiree band put on their mightiest show to date at the iconic Barrowland Ballroom as fans descend on Glasgow for a massive west coast party. Featuring interviews with band members plus concert highlights.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Dàna
Scotland's Wild Side
programme.sub-title: Rònaigh ║ Dàna. S2. ALBAE4/6. Rona ║ Dàna. S2. ALBAE4/6
programme.desc:
Largely unexplored by climbers, the island of Rona offers serious adventure potential to those willing to forego comfort and convenience. In order to seek out unclimbed lines and new routes of their own, Coinneach MacFhraing and Owen Sinclair travel to the island and spend a few days wrestling with wet boots, loose rock and the prospect of returning home empty-handed.
Air eilean far nach deach mòran sreap a dhèanamh roimhe, tha Rònaigh a’ tabhann chothroman air leth spòrsail dhan fheadhainn a tha deònach leigeil às de chomhfurtachd is goireasachd.
A’ sireadh slighean ùra dhaibh fhèin nach deach a shreap roimhe, tha Coinneach MacFhraing agus Owen Sinclair a’ siubhal chun an eilean gus latha no dhà a chur seachad a’ dèiligeadh ri bòtannan fliucha, sgrìodan cloiche agus dòchasach nach till iad dhachaigh gun chàil nan cois.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Coinneach MacFhraing Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Director - Hamish MacLeod.

programme.title: Mòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail
programme.desc:
Tha Cathy NicDhòmhnaill a' toirt thugaibh Là Mòr nan Còisirean Sgìreil bhon Mhòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail ann an Loch Abar. Bidh còisirean a’ cruinneachadh ann an Talla Chonsairt Rìoghail Ghlaschu agus a’ strì airson a’ phrìomh dhuais - Sgiath MhicShimidh agus Thulaich Bhàrdainn. B‘ e Ceòlraidh Ghàidhlig Ghlaschu a choisinn an duais ann an Loch Abar ann an 2025. Bidh còisirean cuideachd a’ farpais airson Cuach Cuimhneachan Mairead NicDhonnchaidh, a bhuannaich Còisir Ghàidhlig Loch Abar ann an 2025.
Bidh dithis eòlaiche còmhla ri Cathy san stiùidio is iad a’ toirt am beachdan seachad air na còisirean bhon dà fharpais. Bidh cothrom ann cuideachd faicinn cò a ghlèidh farpaisean còisir na maidne is Cupan Còisir Ghàidhlig Ghrianaig airson puirt-à-beul agus Geall-dùbhlain Esme Nic a’ Ghobhainn airson mnathan gan toirt seachad, am measg eile.
Cathy MacDonald presents live coverage of the most prestigious choral competitions from the last day of the Royal National Mòd in Glasgow. Area choirs gather in the Glasgow Royal Concert Hall to compete for the Lovat and Tullibardine Shield, which was won by Glasgow Gaelic Musical Association in Lochaber in 2025. Running alongside is the competition for the Margrat Duncan Memorial Trophy, won last year by Lochaber Gaelic Choir.
Cathy is joined in the studio by two expert panellists who offer analysis of both competitions. The programme also features winners of the morning’s choral competitions, which included the Greenock Gaelic Choir Cup for puirt-à-beul and the Esme Smythe Trophy for ladies' voices.

Latha trang eile aig Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche le Ciorstaidh an Loiliopop a’ lìbhrigeadh Là Sàbhailteachd Rathaid agus Danny an Janny trang le Là Sàbhailteachd Teine. Bidh na camarathan againne a’ leantainn a h-uile rud a thachras tron latha.
A hectic day at Sgoil Taobh na Cloiche with Ciorstaidh overseeing Road Safety Day, while Danny is also busy with Fire Safety Day. Our cameras follow all the events of this important day in the school calendar. Mrs Fullerton - Calum Macdonald Kirsty - Ellen Macdonald Danny Janny - Bekah Macleod Narrator - Hannah McKirdy Producer - Sarah MacKinnon.

programme.title: Clo Beag Chirsty Bella
programme.desc:
Tha Chirsty Bella ag iarraidh Clò Hearach a dhèanamh…tha e gu math nas fhasa smaoineachadh air sin na tha e ga chuir an gnìomh. Tha ì a’ fuireach ann an Scalpaigh, Na Hearadh. Tha gaol aice air a h-eilean agus tha ì ga cumail fhèin trang le bhith a reic uighean agus a dèanamh dannsa Gàidheallach. ‘S toigh leatha cuideachd an clò ainmeil clùiteach: Clò Hearach. Tha an t-seann bheairt mar time machine, ga toirt air ais gu lìnn an fhearsaid, nan càrd, ‘s a spàl. An teid orra à clò a dhèanamh ann an àm?
Chirsty Bella wants to produce her own Harris tweed but that is easier said than done. She lives in Scalpay, a little village in the Isle of Harris, loves her island and keeps herself going through little jobs like selling eggs and traditional Scottish Highland dancing. She also loves the famous and traditional fabric: Harris Tweed. The original Harris Tweed loom is like a time machine that takes her back over a hundred years to the age of spindles, combs and shuttles. Will she manage to weave her cloth in time?

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc:
Tha Belle bhochd air a puinnseanachadh. Cò dhèanadh leithid a rud? Uill Anton, sin cò. Tha Sebastian, le taic bho Adele, a' dèanamh a dhìcheall Belle a shàbhaladh 's a tilleadh dhachaigh.
Belle has been poisoned. Who would do such a thing? Anton, that’s who. Sebastian, with help from Adele, does his utmost to save Belle and bring her home. Sebastian - Ellen Macdonald Adele - Mischa Macpherson Jules - Alec MacDonald Anton - Derek Murray Casper - Calum MacKinnon Executive Producer - Bill Macleòid Producer - May Smart Producer - Mairi Macleod Writer - Alec MacDonald.

programme.title: Seonaidh
Shaun the Sheep
programme.sub-title: Tunnag! ║ Seonaidh. S4E22/30. Duck ║ Seonaidh. S4E22/30

When Shaun and the flock discover that a pair of nesting ducks have stolen their bedding to make a comfy new home on top of Bitzer's kennel, the battle is on to set things straight.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra na h-Alba
programme.desc:
Green-fingered Murdo Macdonald visits some of the country’s most important gardens to explore their design, plant-life, setting and history.
Murdo goes to 'The Impossible Garden', Inverewe, on the coast of Wester Ross near Poolewe. He finds out how the unique climate impacts on the plants they are able to grow, including rare Wollemi Pines and insect-eating plants in the Savage Garden. He’ll also find out more about the history of the garden from those who work there now.
Roddy Maclean explains what lichen is and what it tells us about the environment, and Dr Mark Newman of The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh tell us more about insectivorous plants.
Tha gàirneilear sgileil, Murchadh Dòmhnallach, a’ tadhal air cuid de ghàrraidhean mòra na h-Alba, a’coimhead air an cruth, na tha fàs unnta agus an eachdraidh.
Sa phrògram seo tha Murchadh a’tadhal air “Gàrradh Do-dhèanta” – gàrradh Inbir Iù ri cladach Taobh Siar Rois faisg air Poll Iù. Gheibh e mach mun bhuaidh a th’aig an deagh aimsir air na lusan sna craobhan a tha a’fàs aca, leithid giuthas tearc Wollemi, agus, sa Ghàrradh Fhiadhaich, lusan a dh’itheas biastagan. Cluinnidh e cuideachd eachdraidh a’ghàrraidh, bhuapasan a tha ag obair ann an-diugh.
Tha Ruairidh MacIlleathain a’mìneachadh dè th’ann an crotal, agus dè dh’innseas e dhuinn mun àrainneachd, agus tha barrachd aig an Oll. Mark Newman a Gàrradh Luibheanach Rìoghail Dhùn Èidinn ri innse mu dhìtheanan a tha ag ithe chuileagan is eile.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Murdo Macdonald Director - Shona Masson.

programme.title: Cù Leis Thu?
A Puppy for Padruig
programme.desc:
Peter is on a journey to find a perfect companion for his new puppy, Flòraidh, back home in Oban. In this episode, he's considering the labrador retriever and sets out to uncover why it’s Scotland’s most popular breed. His first stop is a farm in Stirlingshire, where he meets a breeder with an adorable litter and learns about the labrador’s origins as a skilled retriever, bred for fetching game from water. Eager to see these dogs in action, Peter heads to South Uist in the Outer Hebrides. Joining a shooting party before sunrise, he watches in awe as labradors plunge into cold waters, retrieving geese with ease and agility.
While Peter can see their appeal for outdoor adventurers, he’s curious about why they’re such popular family pets. To explore, he visits Glasgow to meet some working guide dogs, discovering the breed’s gentle, intelligent, and dependable qualities. Finally, Peter travels to the Isle of Lewis, where his friend Anne and her family showcase life with three labradors, highlighting their adaptability as family companions.
After journeying across Scotland, Peter gains a deep appreciation for labradors, and begins to understand why they hold such a special place in the hearts of so many. But are they the right fit for him?
Tha Pàdraig air turas airson deagh chompanach a lorg dhan chuilean ùr aige, Flòraidh, a th' aig an taigh san Òban. Anns a' phrògram seo, tha e a' beachdachadh air an Labrador retriever, agus a' rannsachadh carson as e an cù as mòr-chòrdte an Alba. Thèid e an toiseach gu tuathanas ann an Siorrachd Shruighlea airson coinneachadh ri neach-briodaidh aig a bheil àl àlainn, agus airson ionnsachadh mu eachdraidh a' choin a chaidh a bhriodadh airson tilleadh le creach às an uisge. Leis gu bheil fadachd air na coin fhaicinn aig an obair, tha e a' dèanamh air Uibhist a Deas. Air a chois le buidheann seilge roimh èirigh na grèine, tha e gan coimhead a' leum dhan uisge fhuar, a' tilleadh le geòidh gu sgiobalta 's gu frogail.
Ged a' thuigeas Pàdruig cho tarraingeach 's a tha iad dha feadhainn a bhios an sàs ann an spòrs a-muigh, carson a tha teaghlaichean co measail orra? Airson faighinn a-mach, tha e a' dol a Ghlaschu a' choinneachadh ri coin-iùil, 's ag ionnsachadh mu bheusan ciùin, ciallach agus earbsach nan con.

programme.title: Tiugainn a Dhannsa
programme.desc:
Thànaig crìoch air earrann de dh'eachdraidh chur-seachadan na Gàidhealtachd is nan Eilean nuair a dhùin tallachan -baile ann an iomadh ceàrnaidh. Chaidh tallachan ur an àrda ach is ann ag amas air feumalachdan ginealach ur a bha iad sin. Tha am prògram seo a' toirt beò a' rithist talla-bhaile. Dìreach mar thogalach sam bith eile tron là ach nuair a thuiteadh an oidhche agus a' thigeadh na brògan dannsa a-mach a bha mar saoghal eile.
Documenting the place of village halls at the heart of communities across Scotland throughout the 20th century. The tearing down of old village halls across the Highlands and Islands marks the end of an era.
Balivanich, Carinish, Acharacle, Lochmaddy, Leverburgh, Shawbost, Vatersay, Aird, Ness, the Highlanders' Institute - many halls have been replaced by buildings which focus their attention on the needs of a very different generation. The programme is illustrated with hilarious and often nostalgic anecdotes of these special places, so small and unimpressive by the light of day, but which were transformed by night into meccas of music and dance.

programme.title: Mòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail
programme.desc:
Air an oidhche mu dheireadh dhen Mòd Nàiseanta Rìoghail ann an Glaschu, tha Cathy NicDhòmhnaill a' toirt thugaibh na còisirean as fheàrr bho na prìomh fharpaisean thairis air an dà latha mu dheireadh. Cluinnear bho na còisirean sgìreil a ghlèidh Sgiath MhicShimidh agus Thulaich Bhàrdainn agus Cuach Cuimhneachan Mairead NicDhonnchaidh. Chithear cuideachd na còisirean a bhuannaich farpaisean nan còisirean dùthchail Diardaoin, nam measg na buidhnean a ghlèidh Sgiath Latharna agus Cuach Cuimhneachan an t-Siorraim MacMhaighstir Caimbeul.
A thuilleadh air na còisirean bidh cothrom eile ann èisdeachd ri na sàr sheinneadairean a ghlèidh Buinn Òir a’ Chomuinn Ghàidhealaich agus Bonn Òir son seinn san t-seann nòs.
Cathy Macdonald brings this year’s coverage of the Royal National Mòd in Glasgow to a close with highlights from the choral competitions held over the last two days.
Featuring songs from entrants who successfully competed for the two main prizes for the area choirs, the Lovat and Tullibardine Shield and the Margrat Duncan Memorial Trophy. Plus a selection winners from the rural choirs competitions, including those who clinched the coveted Lorn Shield and the Sheriff MacMaster Campbell Memorial Quaich.
There will also be another opportunity to hear the talented solo singers who took home the An Comunn Gàidhealach Gold Medal and the Gold Medal for traditional singing.

programme.title: Transatlantic Sessions
programme.desc:
Julie Fowlis agus Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh le taghadh ciùil bho dhà dheichead den phrògram ciùil cliùiteach, ‘Transatlantic Sessions’ ann an cuideachd sàr luchd-ciùil thraidiseanta is dhùthchasach à Alba, Eirinn agus Na SA. Anns a’ phrògram seo, cothrom air measgachadh de stoidhlean ciùil ann an taisbeanaidhean ‘Sessions’ le Eddi Reader, Karan Casey, Cara Dillon, Bruce Molsky agus Ricky Skaggs.
Julie Fowlis and Muireann Nic Amhlaoibh present highlights from two decades of the legendary music show, ‘Transatlantic Sessions’ featuring some of the biggest trad and roots music stars from Scotland, Ireland and the US. programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra na h-Alba
programme.desc:
Green-fingered Murdo Macdonald visits some of the country’s most important gardens to explore their design, plant-life, setting and history.
Murdo goes to 'The Impossible Garden', Inverewe, on the coast of Wester Ross near Poolewe. He finds out how the unique climate impacts on the plants they are able to grow, including rare Wollemi Pines and insect-eating plants in the Savage Garden. He’ll also find out more about the history of the garden from those who work there now.
Roddy Maclean explains what lichen is and what it tells us about the environment, and Dr Mark Newman of The Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh tell us more about insectivorous plants.
Tha gàirneilear sgileil, Murchadh Dòmhnallach, a’ tadhal air cuid de ghàrraidhean mòra na h-Alba, a’coimhead air an cruth, na tha fàs unnta agus an eachdraidh.
Sa phrògram seo tha Murchadh a’tadhal air “Gàrradh Do-dhèanta” – gàrradh Inbir Iù ri cladach Taobh Siar Rois faisg air Poll Iù. Gheibh e mach mun bhuaidh a th’aig an deagh aimsir air na lusan sna craobhan a tha a’fàs aca, leithid giuthas tearc Wollemi, agus, sa Ghàrradh Fhiadhaich, lusan a dh’itheas biastagan. Cluinnidh e cuideachd eachdraidh a’ghàrraidh, bhuapasan a tha ag obair ann an-diugh.
Tha Ruairidh MacIlleathain a’mìneachadh dè th’ann an crotal, agus dè dh’innseas e dhuinn mun àrainneachd, agus tha barrachd aig an Oll. Mark Newman a Gàrradh Luibheanach Rìoghail Dhùn Èidinn ri innse mu dhìtheanan a tha ag ithe chuileagan is eile.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Murdo Macdonald Director - Shona Masson.

programme.title: Dàna
Scotland's Wild Side
programme.sub-title: Rònaigh ║ Dàna. S2. ALBAE4/6. Rona ║ Dàna. S2. ALBAE4/6
programme.desc:
Largely unexplored by climbers, the island of Rona offers serious adventure potential to those willing to forego comfort and convenience. In order to seek out unclimbed lines and new routes of their own, Coinneach MacFhraing and Owen Sinclair travel to the island and spend a few days wrestling with wet boots, loose rock and the prospect of returning home empty-handed.
Air eilean far nach deach mòran sreap a dhèanamh roimhe, tha Rònaigh a’ tabhann chothroman air leth spòrsail dhan fheadhainn a tha deònach leigeil às de chomhfurtachd is goireasachd.
A’ sireadh slighean ùra dhaibh fhèin nach deach a shreap roimhe, tha Coinneach MacFhraing agus Owen Sinclair a’ siubhal chun an eilean gus latha no dhà a chur seachad a’ dèiligeadh ri bòtannan fliucha, sgrìodan cloiche agus dòchasach nach till iad dhachaigh gun chàil nan cois.
In Gaelic with English subtitles. Presenter - Coinneach MacFhraing Executive Producer - Tony Kearney Executive Producer - Jim Webster Executive Producer - Calum McConnell Director - Hamish MacLeod.

programme.title: Cù Leis Thu?
A Puppy for Padruig
programme.desc:
Peter is on a journey to find a perfect companion for his new puppy, Flòraidh, back home in Oban. In this episode, he's considering the labrador retriever and sets out to uncover why it’s Scotland’s most popular breed. His first stop is a farm in Stirlingshire, where he meets a breeder with an adorable litter and learns about the labrador’s origins as a skilled retriever, bred for fetching game from water. Eager to see these dogs in action, Peter heads to South Uist in the Outer Hebrides. Joining a shooting party before sunrise, he watches in awe as labradors plunge into cold waters, retrieving geese with ease and agility.
While Peter can see their appeal for outdoor adventurers, he’s curious about why they’re such popular family pets. To explore, he visits Glasgow to meet some working guide dogs, discovering the breed’s gentle, intelligent, and dependable qualities. Finally, Peter travels to the Isle of Lewis, where his friend Anne and her family showcase life with three labradors, highlighting their adaptability as family companions.
After journeying across Scotland, Peter gains a deep appreciation for labradors, and begins to understand why they hold such a special place in the hearts of so many. But are they the right fit for him?
Tha Pàdraig air turas airson deagh chompanach a lorg dhan chuilean ùr aige, Flòraidh, a th' aig an taigh san Òban. Anns a' phrògram seo, tha e a' beachdachadh air an Labrador retriever, agus a' rannsachadh carson as e an cù as mòr-chòrdte an Alba. Thèid e an toiseach gu tuathanas ann an Siorrachd Shruighlea airson coinneachadh ri neach-briodaidh aig a bheil àl àlainn, agus airson ionnsachadh mu eachdraidh a' choin a chaidh a bhriodadh airson tilleadh le creach às an uisge. Leis gu bheil fadachd air na coin fhaicinn aig an obair, tha e a' dèanamh air Uibhist a Deas. Air a chois le buidheann seilge roimh èirigh na grèine, tha e gan coimhead a' leum dhan uisge fhuar, a' tilleadh le geòidh gu sgiobalta 's gu frogail.
Ged a' thuigeas Pàdruig cho tarraingeach 's a tha iad dha feadhainn a bhios an sàs ann an spòrs a-muigh, carson a tha teaghlaichean co measail orra? Airson faighinn a-mach, tha e a' dol a Ghlaschu a' choinneachadh ri coin-iùil, 's ag ionnsachadh mu bheusan ciùin, ciallach agus earbsach nan con.

programme.title: Trail West is Caraidean aig Barrowland

Cuirm shònraichte bhon Bharrowland Ballroom, le ceòl bho Trail West, Beinn Lee is Ruairidh Gray. A’ comharrachadh 15 bliadhna mar chòmhlan, thug Trail West cuireadh do an caraidean ceòlmhor gu ‘dachaigh rock & roll’ agus rinn an luchd-leantainn an slighe chun an talla-ciùil as cliùitiche ann an Glaschu airson a’ phàrtaidh as fheàrr air a’ Chost’ an Iar.

Celebrating 15 years as a band, Trail West invited their musical pals to 'the home of rock and roll', so their fans descended on Glasgow’s most iconic venue for the ultimate west coast party.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: World Pipe Band Championships
programme.desc:
Tha Catrìona NicNèill air Lèanag Ghlaschu aig Farpais Chòmhlan Pìoba na Cruinne neo Na Worlds mar as fheàrr a dh’aithnichear iad. Thairis air a’ phrògram bidh i a’ toirt thugainn blasad den phìobaireachd ’s den drumaireachd as fheàrr bho air feadh an t-saoghail: à Alba, Èirinn, Èirinn a Tuath, Canada, Aimeireagaidh agus Sealainn Nuadh.
Bha 14 còmhlain a’ farpais aig Ìre a h-Aon am-bliadhna agus chì sibh na seallaidhean as fheàrr bhon dàrna latha. Bhuannaich Còmhlan Pìoba Inbhir Aora agus an Sgìre airson an dàrna turas sreath a chèile fo stiùir Màidsear na Pìoba Stuart Liddell MBE agus Prìomh Dhrumair a’ chòmhlain, Steven McWhirter. Cluinnear cuideachd ceòl bho chòmhlain eile, leithid Field Marshal Montgomery, Shotts agus Dykehead Caledonia agus Manawatu Scottish.
Carrie MacNeil introduces the bands competing at Grade One in the 2025 World Pipe Band Championships, better known as The Worlds. The show features the finest pipers and drummers from Scotland, Ireland, Northern Ireland, Canada and America.
In total, 14 bands competed across the two-day event on Glasgow Green. The programme features selected performances from the second day. Inveraray and District took home the title for the second consecutive year, under the direction of Pipe Major Stuart Liddell MBE and Lead Drummer, Steven McWhirter.
Also featured in the programme are performances from Field Marshal Montgomery, Shotts and Dykehead Caledonia and Manawatu Scottish.
In Gaelic with English subtitles.

Aithnichte airson a dhreach shònraichte folk-punk de dh’òrain aithnichte, choisinn RuMac cliù bho chionn ghoirid air Britain’s Got Talent, agus abair gun robh annas air sluagh Belladrum leis an taisbeanadh accordion gun rian.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift

Joanna Page heads to Bridgend as the show brings its charity shop challenge to south Wales. With just 60 minutes on the clock and £100 each, best friends Anum and Betti go head-to-head to see who can turn second-hand bargains into the biggest profit for charity.
Paired with expert thrifters Pete and Lola, the race begins across Bridgend’s high street, where hidden gems lurk among the rails and shelves. Early excitement over a Burberry outfit raises questions about authenticity, while a pair of striking Christian Louboutin trainers presents a serious dilemma – a potential goldmine or a costly mistake. Betti’s nursery curtains are reworked into a stylish wrap dress, while Anum’s plain wooden jewellery box is transformed into a vibrant, hand-painted statement piece, proving that creativity can dramatically boost value.
Then comes the ultimate test: the live-streamed auction. Nerves are jangling as Anum and Betti step into the spotlight, pitching their items to a live online audience. As bids rise and fall in real time, confidence and charm become just as important as the items themselves. Authenticity checks deliver last-minute twists, and a risky gamble could either decide the winner or wipe out a chunk of their budget.
By the end of a dramatic auction, the profits are counted, surprises are revealed, and one contestant emerges ahead. But the real winner is charity, with all proceeds donated to the contestants’ chosen causes.
Packed with jeopardy, big decisions and satisfying transformations, the visit to Bridgend is a lively, feel-good episode that celebrates second-hand style, creative thinking and the thrill of finding hidden value where others might not look.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc:
Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die.
As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated.
Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death.
Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales.
Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the creative heart of Hebden Bridge – a former mill town famed for its independent spirit and as a filming location for the BBC TV series Happy Valley.
Today’s competitors are friends Emma and Sophie, who first met on a fashion shoot for Dove House Hospice. Now they’re going head-to-head to raise as much money as possible for the charity that brought them together. Guiding them are expert vintage thrifters – and husbands – Tom and Terry.
The teams quickly reveal very different shopping styles. Sophie and Tom dive straight into the nearest shop, where Sophie’s love of oversized menswear leads her to a vintage St Michael jacket – a nostalgic find with added appeal thanks to its 'Made in the UK' label. Emma and Terry take a steadier approach, carefully assessing a rare red rotary dial telephone before building a collection packed with retro charm.
The hunt for Joanna’s pick of the day – an original 1970s Holly Hobbie doll – adds extra jeopardy. While Tom hesitates over the gamble, Sophie trusts her instinct and pushes to secure the collectable toy. As time slips away, Emma and Terry uncover a colourful 1960s picnic set and an eye-catching Murano-style glass duck that divides opinion but promises personality at auction.
For the upcycling challenge, creativity takes centre stage. Emma selects a vintage rocking chair and plans to re-cover it using fabric from animal-illustrated curtains – a bold, characterful refresh. Sophie, however, leaves her upcycle decision perilously late, eventually opting for an unexpected sleeping bag with plans to transform it into a statement padded coat.
The final minutes are frantic for Sophie and Tom, who scramble to spend the remainder of their budget. With Joanna urging them on, they squeeze in a last-second dash for additional vintage finds before they run out of time.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must swap browsing rails for the rostrum. Emma channels calm confidence, while Sophie leans into theatrical flair. With bids climbing and pride on the line, it’s a spirited showdown, but whatever the outcome, Dove House Hospice stands to benefit from a creative, chaotic and thoroughly entertaining day on Hebden Bridge's high street.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc:
Chris and Lee travel to Eton Wick to help Andrew and Angela revive their Victorian cottage garden. Once lovingly maintained, it has now fallen into neglect, with a rotten pergola, a decaying arbour seat and overgrown borders in need of care. The uneven, rough surface also makes the garden unsafe and inaccessible for their young son William.
Andrew and Angela dream of putting their own twist on a traditional Victorian cottage garden with timeless tranquillity and modern functionality. They want to create a beautiful, low-maintenance space that’s also accessible for William, who relies on outdoor time because of his disabilities. The garden will feature smooth, accessible pathways, strategic seating areas and a calming, interactive play zone designed with William’s mobility in mind. A secluded corner filled with soothing plants and comfortable seating will offer the family a place to unwind and reconnect after hospital visits and busy days.
Andrew and Angela met while on holiday in Dublin and have shared a love of travel ever since. Angela, originally from America, and Andrew, a seasoned world traveller himself, settled down when she became pregnant, buying their home to start a family. But life soon took an unexpected turn when their son William was born prematurely with a rare condition, bilateral tibial hemimelia, causing severe malformations in both legs and feet. Their renovation plans were put on hold as hospital visits, surgeries and recoveries became part of everyday life. Earlier this year, William underwent an amputation of his right leg and is now learning to walk confidently with his prosthetic. Three further surgeries on his left leg are planned, with more likely into his early twenties.
Despite these challenges, Andrew and Angela remain optimistic and determined to create a safe, tranquil and joyful outdoor space where William can play and the family can relax together.
Can Chris and Lee craft a Victorian haven garden, one that blends charm, accessibility and serenity, on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Rose Ayling-Ellis came to fame on EastEnders and captured the nation’s hearts when she won Strictly. Since then, she’s used her platform to campaign for deaf rights. Now, Rose goes in search of her family history. She’s heard a rumour of Italian ancestry on her father’s side and is hoping for a bit of drama on her mum’s.
Rose starts by visiting her mum in Kent. Rose’s mum has an intriguing picture of Rose’s three-time great-grandmother. The family story is that she ran a pub in Birmingham with an iron fist. But Rose’s mum doesn’t know her name or if any of the stories are true. To find out, Rose heads to Birmingham.
Local historian Simon Briercliffe helps Rose put a name to her three-time great-grandmother – Agnes Chilton. Trade directories and census returns show that Agnes and her husband Alfred ran a pub. A local newspaper article tells a story worthy of an EastEnders plotline: Agnes and Alfred were caught up in an altercation with a customer, resulting in a court appearance. Rose discovers that Alfred died aged 48, leaving Agnes a widow. Fearing the worst for a woman on her own at that time, Rose is happy to discover that shortly after Alfred’s death Agnes moved to her own pub, the Aston Tavern.
Rose heads there to meet historian Professor Julie-Marie Strange and discovers that Agnes married again at the age of 50. However, two years later, Agnes’s second husband also died. Once again, Agnes was undeterred and expanded the pub further. Rose is delighted to find out that the current landlord of the Aston Tavern has named the rooms after former landlords, including Agnes. As Rose goes to find the room named after her ancestor, she reflects on what a resilient woman Agnes was.
Rose then turns to the paternal side of the family. At her dad’s house in Somerset, Rose’s grandma tells her that her father, Rose’s great-grandad, came from a huge family of 17 children. She doesn’t know a lot about them but remembers that her grandfather, James Welland, Rose’s great-great-grandad, lost his hand in an accident, and she also recalls her dad telling her that when he was a child, they were very poor and lived in a squat in Exeter. Rose also asks about the Italian connection. Rose’s dad explains that this story came through his dad’s side of the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads west to the seaside town of Aberystwyth, famous for its Victorian pier and unpredictable weather. Battling the rain are mother-and-son duo Margaret and Endaf, both hoping their shared love of a bargain will translate into serious profit for charity.
With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they’re paired with expert thrifters and sent racing around Aberystwyth’s charity shops. Endaf starts strongly, snapping up a quality blazer for under a tenner before confidently adding crystal glasses and rare Babycham glasses to his haul. He later spots a vintage wool-and-cashmere jacket, Joanna’s pick of the day, and takes a chance on a violin, proving he is willing to think outside the box.
Margaret, meanwhile, wastes no time securing her upcycle item – a nest of dark wood tables bought for just £3. She also picks up Dutch wooden clogs, a vintage leather messenger bag and gambles on an expensive suede jacket, carefully selecting items she believes have strong resale appeal. The contest has a warm but competitive family dynamic, with playful rivalry building between mum and son as the clock ticks down.
At the transformation stage, Endaf’s plain 80s leather jacket is dramatically reworked with fabric paint and new gold hardware by upcycle entrepreneur Emma Deeks, turning it into a bold statement piece. Margaret’s modest £3 tables are transformed by using a poured-paint technique, creating a colourful, marbled finish that completely reinvents them.
Then comes the live-streamed auction. Endaf grows in confidence as he pitches his items, using detail and humour to drive bids higher, especially on the vintage Burton jacket and his upcycled leather piece. Margaret charms viewers with her warmth and storytelling, successfully selling her clogs and making a strong profit on her upcycled tables.
When the totals are combined with their online sales, who will win between mother and son? The real triumph is for their chosen charity, the British Heart Foundation, with an impressive amount raised in total.
Rain-soaked, good-humoured and full of personality, this contest is a heartwarming family face-off that proves thrifting talent might just run in the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to Bridgend as the show brings its charity shop challenge to south Wales. With just 60 minutes on the clock and £100 each, best friends Anum and Betti go head-to-head to see who can turn second-hand bargains into the biggest profit for charity.
Paired with expert thrifters Pete and Lola, the race begins across Bridgend’s high street, where hidden gems lurk among the rails and shelves. Anum is drawn to vintage bric-a-brac and collectibles, snapping up teapots, crockery and curios, while Betti focuses on fashion, spotting bold fabrics, statement pieces and high-end labels.
But not every bargain is what it seems. Early excitement over a Burberry outfit raises questions about authenticity, while a pair of striking Christian Louboutin trainers presents a serious dilemma – a potential goldmine or a costly mistake. With the clock ticking and budgets shrinking, both teams must decide how much risk they are willing to take.
Once the shopping frenzy ends, attention turns to transformation. Each contestant chooses one item to be upcycled by expert makers. Betti’s nursery curtains are reworked into a stylish wrap dress, while Anum’s plain wooden jewellery box is transformed into a vibrant, hand-painted statement piece, proving that creativity can dramatically boost value.
Then comes the ultimate test: the live-streamed auction. Nerves are jangling as Anum and Betti step into the spotlight, pitching their items to a live online audience. As bids rise and fall in real time, confidence and charm become just as important as the items themselves. Authenticity checks deliver last-minute twists, and a risky gamble could either decide the winner or wipe out a chunk of their budget.
By the end of a dramatic auction, the profits are counted, surprises are revealed, and one contestant emerges ahead. But the real winner is charity, with all proceeds donated to the contestants’ chosen causes.
Packed with jeopardy, big decisions and satisfying transformations, the visit to Bridgend is a lively, feel-good episode that celebrates second-hand style, creative thinking and the thrill of finding hidden value where others might not look.

programme.desc:
Joanna Page travels to the quintessential Somerset town of Midsomer Norton, where the river Somer and a famous connection to TV murder mysteries set the stage for a high-stakes thrifting challenge. Polly and Pete stay local, quickly uncovering high-end treasures like a pair of brand new Church’s boots for a bargain price and a vintage Next jacket. Despite some first shop nerves from Callum, they manage to sniff out Joanna's pick of the day – a Manhattan portage bag – and a set of art deco glasses.
The competition intensifies during the upcycling phase. Polly’s £6 pink eiderdown is transformed into a trendy, one-of-a-kind quilted jacket. Callum, spurred on by a bit of spite to outdo Polly, invests half his budget in a Stag Minstrel dressing table. Furniture artist Sarah Haugh gives it a modern, show-stopping makeover with bold stencilling.
On auction day, the atmosphere is electric. Polly proves to be a natural at salesmanship, even getting Joanna to model her upcycled jacket to drive up bids. Callum struggles with a severe case of the shakes, but once he gains his confidence and starts sharing the history of his finds, the money begins to fly in. With the live auction totals and online sales combined, the final result is a travesty for one but a triumph for the other. In the end, the real winner is the charity, with an impressive amount raised through savvy scouting and creative restoration. programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc:
Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die.
As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated.
Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death.
Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales.
Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height. He’s part of a wave of young men boosting their testosterone to get pumped bodies and appear as manly as possible to the opposite sex. She then discovers that this particular social craze may not be so modern after all as she follows a trail that leads her to Wolverhampton Wanderers and a bizarre revelation that the FA Cup final in 1939 was nicknamed the 'Monkey Gland Final' after several players had testosterone-boosting injections before the game.
Migraines can be so severe that they trigger headaches and vomiting that last for hours, so Stacey is intrigued by a social trend that claims they can be cured by a fast food meal. She explores with the doctors if there could be a kernel of scientific truth in the claims. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the creative heart of Hebden Bridge – a former mill town famed for its independent spirit and as a filming location for the BBC TV series Happy Valley.
Today’s competitors are friends Emma and Sophie, who first met on a fashion shoot for Dove House Hospice. Now they’re going head-to-head to raise as much money as possible for the charity that brought them together. Guiding them are expert vintage thrifters – and husbands – Tom and Terry.
The teams quickly reveal very different shopping styles. Sophie and Tom dive straight into the nearest shop, where Sophie’s love of oversized menswear leads her to a vintage St Michael jacket – a nostalgic find with added appeal thanks to its 'Made in the UK' label. Emma and Terry take a steadier approach, carefully assessing a rare red rotary dial telephone before building a collection packed with retro charm.
The hunt for Joanna’s pick of the day – an original 1970s Holly Hobbie doll – adds extra jeopardy. While Tom hesitates over the gamble, Sophie trusts her instinct and pushes to secure the collectable toy. As time slips away, Emma and Terry uncover a colourful 1960s picnic set and an eye-catching Murano-style glass duck that divides opinion but promises personality at auction.
For the upcycling challenge, creativity takes centre stage. Emma selects a vintage rocking chair and plans to re-cover it using fabric from animal-illustrated curtains – a bold, characterful refresh. Sophie, however, leaves her upcycle decision perilously late, eventually opting for an unexpected sleeping bag with plans to transform it into a statement padded coat.
The final minutes are frantic for Sophie and Tom, who scramble to spend the remainder of their budget. With Joanna urging them on, they squeeze in a last-second dash for additional vintage finds before they run out of time.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must swap browsing rails for the rostrum. Emma channels calm confidence, while Sophie leans into theatrical flair. With bids climbing and pride on the line, it’s a spirited showdown, but whatever the outcome, Dove House Hospice stands to benefit from a creative, chaotic and thoroughly entertaining day on Hebden Bridge's high street.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc:
Chris and Lee travel to Eton Wick to help Andrew and Angela revive their Victorian cottage garden. Once lovingly maintained, it has now fallen into neglect, with a rotten pergola, a decaying arbour seat and overgrown borders in need of care. The uneven, rough surface also makes the garden unsafe and inaccessible for their young son William.
Andrew and Angela dream of putting their own twist on a traditional Victorian cottage garden with timeless tranquillity and modern functionality. They want to create a beautiful, low-maintenance space that’s also accessible for William, who relies on outdoor time because of his disabilities. The garden will feature smooth, accessible pathways, strategic seating areas and a calming, interactive play zone designed with William’s mobility in mind. A secluded corner filled with soothing plants and comfortable seating will offer the family a place to unwind and reconnect after hospital visits and busy days.
Andrew and Angela met while on holiday in Dublin and have shared a love of travel ever since. Angela, originally from America, and Andrew, a seasoned world traveller himself, settled down when she became pregnant, buying their home to start a family. But life soon took an unexpected turn when their son William was born prematurely with a rare condition, bilateral tibial hemimelia, causing severe malformations in both legs and feet. Their renovation plans were put on hold as hospital visits, surgeries and recoveries became part of everyday life. Earlier this year, William underwent an amputation of his right leg and is now learning to walk confidently with his prosthetic. Three further surgeries on his left leg are planned, with more likely into his early twenties.
Despite these challenges, Andrew and Angela remain optimistic and determined to create a safe, tranquil and joyful outdoor space where William can play and the family can relax together.
Can Chris and Lee craft a Victorian haven garden, one that blends charm, accessibility and serenity, on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Rose Ayling-Ellis came to fame on EastEnders and captured the nation’s hearts when she won Strictly. Since then, she’s used her platform to campaign for deaf rights. Now, Rose goes in search of her family history. She’s heard a rumour of Italian ancestry on her father’s side and is hoping for a bit of drama on her mum’s.
Rose starts by visiting her mum in Kent. Rose’s mum has an intriguing picture of Rose’s three-time great-grandmother. The family story is that she ran a pub in Birmingham with an iron fist. But Rose’s mum doesn’t know her name or if any of the stories are true. To find out, Rose heads to Birmingham.
Local historian Simon Briercliffe helps Rose put a name to her three-time great-grandmother – Agnes Chilton. Trade directories and census returns show that Agnes and her husband Alfred ran a pub. A local newspaper article tells a story worthy of an EastEnders plotline: Agnes and Alfred were caught up in an altercation with a customer, resulting in a court appearance. Rose discovers that Alfred died aged 48, leaving Agnes a widow. Fearing the worst for a woman on her own at that time, Rose is happy to discover that shortly after Alfred’s death Agnes moved to her own pub, the Aston Tavern.
Rose heads there to meet historian Professor Julie-Marie Strange and discovers that Agnes married again at the age of 50. However, two years later, Agnes’s second husband also died. Once again, Agnes was undeterred and expanded the pub further. Rose is delighted to find out that the current landlord of the Aston Tavern has named the rooms after former landlords, including Agnes. As Rose goes to find the room named after her ancestor, she reflects on what a resilient woman Agnes was.
Rose then turns to the paternal side of the family. At her dad’s house in Somerset, Rose’s grandma tells her that her father, Rose’s great-grandad, came from a huge family of 17 children. She doesn’t know a lot about them but remembers that her grandfather, James Welland, Rose’s great-great-grandad, lost his hand in an accident, and she also recalls her dad telling her that when he was a child, they were very poor and lived in a squat in Exeter. Rose also asks about the Italian connection. Rose’s dad explains that this story came through his dad’s side of the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads west to the seaside town of Aberystwyth, famous for its Victorian pier and unpredictable weather. Battling the rain are mother-and-son duo Margaret and Endaf, both hoping their shared love of a bargain will translate into serious profit for charity.
With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they’re paired with expert thrifters and sent racing around Aberystwyth’s charity shops. Endaf starts strongly, snapping up a quality blazer for under a tenner before confidently adding crystal glasses and rare Babycham glasses to his haul. He later spots a vintage wool-and-cashmere jacket, Joanna’s pick of the day, and takes a chance on a violin, proving he is willing to think outside the box.
Margaret, meanwhile, wastes no time securing her upcycle item – a nest of dark wood tables bought for just £3. She also picks up Dutch wooden clogs, a vintage leather messenger bag and gambles on an expensive suede jacket, carefully selecting items she believes have strong resale appeal. The contest has a warm but competitive family dynamic, with playful rivalry building between mum and son as the clock ticks down.
At the transformation stage, Endaf’s plain 80s leather jacket is dramatically reworked with fabric paint and new gold hardware by upcycle entrepreneur Emma Deeks, turning it into a bold statement piece. Margaret’s modest £3 tables are transformed by using a poured-paint technique, creating a colourful, marbled finish that completely reinvents them.
Then comes the live-streamed auction. Endaf grows in confidence as he pitches his items, using detail and humour to drive bids higher, especially on the vintage Burton jacket and his upcycled leather piece. Margaret charms viewers with her warmth and storytelling, successfully selling her clogs and making a strong profit on her upcycled tables.
When the totals are combined with their online sales, who will win between mother and son? The real triumph is for their chosen charity, the British Heart Foundation, with an impressive amount raised in total.
Rain-soaked, good-humoured and full of personality, this contest is a heartwarming family face-off that proves thrifting talent might just run in the family.

programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to Bridgend as the show brings its charity shop challenge to south Wales. With just 60 minutes on the clock and £100 each, best friends Anum and Betti go head-to-head to see who can turn second-hand bargains into the biggest profit for charity.
Paired with expert thrifters Pete and Lola, the race begins across Bridgend’s high street, where hidden gems lurk among the rails and shelves. Anum is drawn to vintage bric-a-brac and collectibles, snapping up teapots, crockery and curios, while Betti focuses on fashion, spotting bold fabrics, statement pieces and high-end labels.
But not every bargain is what it seems. Early excitement over a Burberry outfit raises questions about authenticity, while a pair of striking Christian Louboutin trainers presents a serious dilemma – a potential goldmine or a costly mistake. With the clock ticking and budgets shrinking, both teams must decide how much risk they are willing to take.
Once the shopping frenzy ends, attention turns to transformation. Each contestant chooses one item to be upcycled by expert makers. Betti’s nursery curtains are reworked into a stylish wrap dress, while Anum’s plain wooden jewellery box is transformed into a vibrant, hand-painted statement piece, proving that creativity can dramatically boost value.
Then comes the ultimate test: the live-streamed auction. Nerves are jangling as Anum and Betti step into the spotlight, pitching their items to a live online audience. As bids rise and fall in real time, confidence and charm become just as important as the items themselves. Authenticity checks deliver last-minute twists, and a risky gamble could either decide the winner or wipe out a chunk of their budget.
By the end of a dramatic auction, the profits are counted, surprises are revealed, and one contestant emerges ahead. But the real winner is charity, with all proceeds donated to the contestants’ chosen causes.
Packed with jeopardy, big decisions and satisfying transformations, the visit to Bridgend is a lively, feel-good episode that celebrates second-hand style, creative thinking and the thrill of finding hidden value where others might not look.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc:
Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die.
As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated.
Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death.
Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales.
Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height. He’s part of a wave of young men boosting their testosterone to get pumped bodies and appear as manly as possible to the opposite sex. But this boost might just be skin-deep, as Stacey explores evidence suggesting long-term use can permanently lower your sperm count and even risks shrinking your testicles.
She then discovers that this particular social craze may not be so modern after all as she follows a trail that leads her to Wolverhampton Wanderers and a bizarre revelation that the FA Cup final in 1939 was nicknamed the 'Monkey Gland Final' after several players had testosterone-boosting injections before the game.
Migraines can be so severe that they trigger headaches and vomiting that last for hours, so Stacey is intrigued by a social trend that claims they can be cured by a fast food meal. She explores with the doctors if there could be a kernel of scientific truth in the claims. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the creative heart of Hebden Bridge – a former mill town famed for its independent spirit and as a filming location for the BBC TV series Happy Valley.
Today’s competitors are friends Emma and Sophie, who first met on a fashion shoot for Dove House Hospice. Now they’re going head-to-head to raise as much money as possible for the charity that brought them together. Guiding them are expert vintage thrifters – and husbands – Tom and Terry.
The teams quickly reveal very different shopping styles. Sophie and Tom dive straight into the nearest shop, where Sophie’s love of oversized menswear leads her to a vintage St Michael jacket – a nostalgic find with added appeal thanks to its 'Made in the UK' label. Emma and Terry take a steadier approach, carefully assessing a rare red rotary dial telephone before building a collection packed with retro charm.
The hunt for Joanna’s pick of the day – an original 1970s Holly Hobbie doll – adds extra jeopardy. While Tom hesitates over the gamble, Sophie trusts her instinct and pushes to secure the collectable toy. As time slips away, Emma and Terry uncover a colourful 1960s picnic set and an eye-catching Murano-style glass duck that divides opinion but promises personality at auction.
For the upcycling challenge, creativity takes centre stage. Emma selects a vintage rocking chair and plans to re-cover it using fabric from animal-illustrated curtains – a bold, characterful refresh. Sophie, however, leaves her upcycle decision perilously late, eventually opting for an unexpected sleeping bag with plans to transform it into a statement padded coat.
The final minutes are frantic for Sophie and Tom, who scramble to spend the remainder of their budget. With Joanna urging them on, they squeeze in a last-second dash for additional vintage finds before they run out of time.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must swap browsing rails for the rostrum. Emma channels calm confidence, while Sophie leans into theatrical flair. With bids climbing and pride on the line, it’s a spirited showdown, but whatever the outcome, Dove House Hospice stands to benefit from a creative, chaotic and thoroughly entertaining day on Hebden Bridge's high street.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc:
Chris and Lee travel to Eton Wick to help Andrew and Angela revive their Victorian cottage garden. Once lovingly maintained, it has now fallen into neglect, with a rotten pergola, a decaying arbour seat and overgrown borders in need of care. The uneven, rough surface also makes the garden unsafe and inaccessible for their young son William.
Andrew and Angela dream of putting their own twist on a traditional Victorian cottage garden with timeless tranquillity and modern functionality. They want to create a beautiful, low-maintenance space that’s also accessible for William, who relies on outdoor time because of his disabilities. The garden will feature smooth, accessible pathways, strategic seating areas and a calming, interactive play zone designed with William’s mobility in mind. A secluded corner filled with soothing plants and comfortable seating will offer the family a place to unwind and reconnect after hospital visits and busy days.
Andrew and Angela met while on holiday in Dublin and have shared a love of travel ever since. Angela, originally from America, and Andrew, a seasoned world traveller himself, settled down when she became pregnant, buying their home to start a family. But life soon took an unexpected turn when their son William was born prematurely with a rare condition, bilateral tibial hemimelia, causing severe malformations in both legs and feet. Their renovation plans were put on hold as hospital visits, surgeries and recoveries became part of everyday life. Earlier this year, William underwent an amputation of his right leg and is now learning to walk confidently with his prosthetic. Three further surgeries on his left leg are planned, with more likely into his early twenties.
Despite these challenges, Andrew and Angela remain optimistic and determined to create a safe, tranquil and joyful outdoor space where William can play and the family can relax together.
Can Chris and Lee craft a Victorian haven garden, one that blends charm, accessibility and serenity, on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Rose Ayling-Ellis came to fame on EastEnders and captured the nation’s hearts when she won Strictly. Since then, she’s used her platform to campaign for deaf rights. Now, Rose goes in search of her family history. She’s heard a rumour of Italian ancestry on her father’s side and is hoping for a bit of drama on her mum’s.
Rose starts by visiting her mum in Kent. Rose’s mum has an intriguing picture of Rose’s three-time great-grandmother. The family story is that she ran a pub in Birmingham with an iron fist. But Rose’s mum doesn’t know her name or if any of the stories are true. To find out, Rose heads to Birmingham.
Local historian Simon Briercliffe helps Rose put a name to her three-time great-grandmother – Agnes Chilton. Trade directories and census returns show that Agnes and her husband Alfred ran a pub. A local newspaper article tells a story worthy of an EastEnders plotline: Agnes and Alfred were caught up in an altercation with a customer, resulting in a court appearance. Rose discovers that Alfred died aged 48, leaving Agnes a widow. Fearing the worst for a woman on her own at that time, Rose is happy to discover that shortly after Alfred’s death Agnes moved to her own pub, the Aston Tavern.
Rose heads there to meet historian Professor Julie-Marie Strange and discovers that Agnes married again at the age of 50. However, two years later, Agnes’s second husband also died. Once again, Agnes was undeterred and expanded the pub further. Rose is delighted to find out that the current landlord of the Aston Tavern has named the rooms after former landlords, including Agnes. As Rose goes to find the room named after her ancestor, she reflects on what a resilient woman Agnes was.
Rose then turns to the paternal side of the family. At her dad’s house in Somerset, Rose’s grandma tells her that her father, Rose’s great-grandad, came from a huge family of 17 children. She doesn’t know a lot about them but remembers that her grandfather, James Welland, Rose’s great-great-grandad, lost his hand in an accident, and she also recalls her dad telling her that when he was a child, they were very poor and lived in a squat in Exeter. Rose also asks about the Italian connection. Rose’s dad explains that this story came through his dad’s side of the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads west to the seaside town of Aberystwyth, famous for its Victorian pier and unpredictable weather. Battling the rain are mother-and-son duo Margaret and Endaf, both hoping their shared love of a bargain will translate into serious profit for charity.
With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they’re paired with expert thrifters and sent racing around Aberystwyth’s charity shops. Endaf starts strongly, snapping up a quality blazer for under a tenner before confidently adding crystal glasses and rare Babycham glasses to his haul. He later spots a vintage wool-and-cashmere jacket, Joanna’s pick of the day, and takes a chance on a violin, proving he is willing to think outside the box.
Margaret, meanwhile, wastes no time securing her upcycle item – a nest of dark wood tables bought for just £3. She also picks up Dutch wooden clogs, a vintage leather messenger bag and gambles on an expensive suede jacket, carefully selecting items she believes have strong resale appeal. The contest has a warm but competitive family dynamic, with playful rivalry building between mum and son as the clock ticks down.
At the transformation stage, Endaf’s plain 80s leather jacket is dramatically reworked with fabric paint and new gold hardware by upcycle entrepreneur Emma Deeks, turning it into a bold statement piece. Margaret’s modest £3 tables are transformed by using a poured-paint technique, creating a colourful, marbled finish that completely reinvents them.
Then comes the live-streamed auction. Endaf grows in confidence as he pitches his items, using detail and humour to drive bids higher, especially on the vintage Burton jacket and his upcycled leather piece. Margaret charms viewers with her warmth and storytelling, successfully selling her clogs and making a strong profit on her upcycled tables.
When the totals are combined with their online sales, who will win between mother and son? The real triumph is for their chosen charity, the British Heart Foundation, with an impressive amount raised in total.
Rain-soaked, good-humoured and full of personality, this contest is a heartwarming family face-off that proves thrifting talent might just run in the family.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to Bridgend as the show brings its charity shop challenge to south Wales. With just 60 minutes on the clock and £100 each, best friends Anum and Betti go head-to-head to see who can turn second-hand bargains into the biggest profit for charity.
Paired with expert thrifters Pete and Lola, the race begins across Bridgend’s high street, where hidden gems lurk among the rails and shelves. Anum is drawn to vintage bric-a-brac and collectibles, snapping up teapots, crockery and curios, while Betti focuses on fashion, spotting bold fabrics, statement pieces and high-end labels.
But not every bargain is what it seems. Early excitement over a Burberry outfit raises questions about authenticity, while a pair of striking Christian Louboutin trainers presents a serious dilemma – a potential goldmine or a costly mistake. With the clock ticking and budgets shrinking, both teams must decide how much risk they are willing to take.
Once the shopping frenzy ends, attention turns to transformation. Each contestant chooses one item to be upcycled by expert makers. Betti’s nursery curtains are reworked into a stylish wrap dress, while Anum’s plain wooden jewellery box is transformed into a vibrant, hand-painted statement piece, proving that creativity can dramatically boost value.
Then comes the ultimate test: the live-streamed auction. Nerves are jangling as Anum and Betti step into the spotlight, pitching their items to a live online audience. As bids rise and fall in real time, confidence and charm become just as important as the items themselves. Authenticity checks deliver last-minute twists, and a risky gamble could either decide the winner or wipe out a chunk of their budget.
By the end of a dramatic auction, the profits are counted, surprises are revealed, and one contestant emerges ahead. But the real winner is charity, with all proceeds donated to the contestants’ chosen causes.
Packed with jeopardy, big decisions and satisfying transformations, the visit to Bridgend is a lively, feel-good episode that celebrates second-hand style, creative thinking and the thrill of finding hidden value where others might not look.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc:
Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die.
As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated.
Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death.
Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales.
Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height.
