programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the creative heart of Hebden Bridge – a former mill town famed for its independent spirit and as a filming location for the BBC TV series Happy Valley.
Today’s competitors are friends Emma and Sophie, who first met on a fashion shoot for Dove House Hospice. Now they’re going head-to-head to raise as much money as possible for the charity that brought them together. Guiding them are expert vintage thrifters – and husbands – Tom and Terry.
The teams quickly reveal very different shopping styles. Sophie and Tom dive straight into the nearest shop, where Sophie’s love of oversized menswear leads her to a vintage St Michael jacket – a nostalgic find with added appeal thanks to its 'Made in the UK' label. Emma and Terry take a steadier approach, carefully assessing a rare red rotary dial telephone before building a collection packed with retro charm.
The hunt for Joanna’s pick of the day – an original 1970s Holly Hobbie doll – adds extra jeopardy. While Tom hesitates over the gamble, Sophie trusts her instinct and pushes to secure the collectable toy. As time slips away, Emma and Terry uncover a colourful 1960s picnic set and an eye-catching Murano-style glass duck that divides opinion but promises personality at auction.
For the upcycling challenge, creativity takes centre stage. Emma selects a vintage rocking chair and plans to re-cover it using fabric from animal-illustrated curtains – a bold, characterful refresh. Sophie, however, leaves her upcycle decision perilously late, eventually opting for an unexpected sleeping bag with plans to transform it into a statement padded coat.
The final minutes are frantic for Sophie and Tom, who scramble to spend the remainder of their budget. With Joanna urging them on, they squeeze in a last-second dash for additional vintage finds before they run out of time.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must swap browsing rails for the rostrum. Emma channels calm confidence, while Sophie leans into theatrical flair. With bids climbing and pride on the line, it’s a spirited showdown, but whatever the outcome, Dove House Hospice stands to benefit from a creative, chaotic and thoroughly entertaining day on Hebden Bridge's high street.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc:
Chris and Lee travel to Eton Wick to help Andrew and Angela revive their Victorian cottage garden. Once lovingly maintained, it has now fallen into neglect, with a rotten pergola, a decaying arbour seat and overgrown borders in need of care. The uneven, rough surface also makes the garden unsafe and inaccessible for their young son William.
Andrew and Angela dream of putting their own twist on a traditional Victorian cottage garden with timeless tranquillity and modern functionality. They want to create a beautiful, low-maintenance space that’s also accessible for William, who relies on outdoor time because of his disabilities. The garden will feature smooth, accessible pathways, strategic seating areas and a calming, interactive play zone designed with William’s mobility in mind. A secluded corner filled with soothing plants and comfortable seating will offer the family a place to unwind and reconnect after hospital visits and busy days.
Andrew and Angela met while on holiday in Dublin and have shared a love of travel ever since. Angela, originally from America, and Andrew, a seasoned world traveller himself, settled down when she became pregnant, buying their home to start a family. But life soon took an unexpected turn when their son William was born prematurely with a rare condition, bilateral tibial hemimelia, causing severe malformations in both legs and feet. Their renovation plans were put on hold as hospital visits, surgeries and recoveries became part of everyday life. Earlier this year, William underwent an amputation of his right leg and is now learning to walk confidently with his prosthetic. Three further surgeries on his left leg are planned, with more likely into his early twenties.
Despite these challenges, Andrew and Angela remain optimistic and determined to create a safe, tranquil and joyful outdoor space where William can play and the family can relax together.
Can Chris and Lee craft a Victorian haven garden, one that blends charm, accessibility and serenity, on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Rose Ayling-Ellis came to fame on EastEnders and captured the nation’s hearts when she won Strictly. Since then, she’s used her platform to campaign for deaf rights. Now, Rose goes in search of her family history. She’s heard a rumour of Italian ancestry on her father’s side and is hoping for a bit of drama on her mum’s.
Rose starts by visiting her mum in Kent. Rose’s mum has an intriguing picture of Rose’s three-time great-grandmother. The family story is that she ran a pub in Birmingham with an iron fist. But Rose’s mum doesn’t know her name or if any of the stories are true. To find out, Rose heads to Birmingham.
Local historian Simon Briercliffe helps Rose put a name to her three-time great-grandmother – Agnes Chilton. Trade directories and census returns show that Agnes and her husband Alfred ran a pub. A local newspaper article tells a story worthy of an EastEnders plotline: Agnes and Alfred were caught up in an altercation with a customer, resulting in a court appearance. Rose discovers that Alfred died aged 48, leaving Agnes a widow. Fearing the worst for a woman on her own at that time, Rose is happy to discover that shortly after Alfred’s death Agnes moved to her own pub, the Aston Tavern.
Rose heads there to meet historian Professor Julie-Marie Strange and discovers that Agnes married again at the age of 50. However, two years later, Agnes’s second husband also died. Once again, Agnes was undeterred and expanded the pub further. Rose is delighted to find out that the current landlord of the Aston Tavern has named the rooms after former landlords, including Agnes. As Rose goes to find the room named after her ancestor, she reflects on what a resilient woman Agnes was.
Rose then turns to the paternal side of the family. At her dad’s house in Somerset, Rose’s grandma tells her that her father, Rose’s great-grandad, came from a huge family of 17 children. She doesn’t know a lot about them but remembers that her grandfather, James Welland, Rose’s great-great-grandad, lost his hand in an accident, and she also recalls her dad telling her that when he was a child, they were very poor and lived in a squat in Exeter. Rose also asks about the Italian connection. Rose’s dad explains that this story came through his dad’s side of the family.

Joanna Page heads west to the seaside town of Aberystwyth, famous for its Victorian pier and unpredictable weather. Battling the rain are mother-and-son duo Margaret and Endaf, both hoping their shared love of a bargain will translate into serious profit for charity.
With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they’re paired with expert thrifters and sent racing around Aberystwyth’s charity shops. Endaf starts strongly, snapping up a quality blazer for under a tenner before confidently adding crystal glasses and rare Babycham glasses to his haul. He later spots a vintage wool-and-cashmere jacket, Joanna’s pick of the day, and takes a chance on a violin, proving he is willing to think outside the box.
Margaret, meanwhile, wastes no time securing her upcycle item – a nest of dark wood tables bought for just £3. She also picks up Dutch wooden clogs, a vintage leather messenger bag and gambles on an expensive suede jacket, carefully selecting items she believes have strong resale appeal. The contest has a warm but competitive family dynamic, with playful rivalry building between mum and son as the clock ticks down.
At the transformation stage, Endaf’s plain 80s leather jacket is dramatically reworked with fabric paint and new gold hardware by upcycle entrepreneur Emma Deeks, turning it into a bold statement piece. Margaret’s modest £3 tables are transformed by using a poured-paint technique, creating a colourful, marbled finish that completely reinvents them.
Then comes the live-streamed auction. Endaf grows in confidence as he pitches his items, using detail and humour to drive bids higher, especially on the vintage Burton jacket and his upcycled leather piece. Margaret charms viewers with her warmth and storytelling, successfully selling her clogs and making a strong profit on her upcycled tables.
When the totals are combined with their online sales, who will win between mother and son? The real triumph is for their chosen charity, the British Heart Foundation, with an impressive amount raised in total.
Rain-soaked, good-humoured and full of personality, this contest is a heartwarming family face-off that proves thrifting talent might just run in the family.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Top of the Pops
programme.desc:
The nation grew up with Top of the Pops, and it was always a talking point, but 35 years ago, a particular kind of Top of the Pops programme and tone held sway. This documentary explores Top of the Pops in 1976 - as a barometer of the state of pop and light entertainment TV.
It celebrates the power of the programme and observes the British society of the mid-70s, British TV and the British pop scene. In 1976, glam was over and nothing had replaced it - the charts belonged to Showaddywaddy, Brotherhood of Man and The Wurzels, all to be found on Top of the Pops hosted by the Radio 1 DJs. If you wanted rock, you looked to the Old Grey Whistle Test, while outside the charts, a new scene was rumbling.

programme.title: Pilgrimage
programme.desc:
It’s the final episode and the pilgrims’ second week. Today, they start just outside Eryri national park and head west towards the Llyn Peninsula and the village of Y Fron in the famous north Wales slate landscape. They have a tough day of hill walking in the rain ahead of them. Tom and Spencer join Sonali on a 24-hour fast to celebrate the start of Paryushan, the holiest festival in the Jain calendar.
The following day, the Pilgrim’s Way takes them through the spectacular slate landscape of the Nantlle valley, a Unesco world heritage site, before they head to St Beuno’s church in Clynnog Fawr - an imposing medieval pilgrim church, where it’s said St Beuno was buried. The pilgrims find their overnight accommodation at a Buddhist meditation and retreat centre, where they’re met by Tara, one of the spiritual leaders.
The following morning, Tara leads them in meditation, before taking the pilgrims on one of the local pilgrimage routes to an ancient holy well, dedicated to Cybi, a 6th-century Celtic early Christian saint. As she lights incense, Tara explains that the Buddhist tradition is to come to places that are known as sacred, and to add their own practices and prayers. When they return to the hermitage, the pilgrims meet Lama Shenpen, its founder and spiritual leader. An extraordinary conversation about Buddhism and a ritual around the stupa – a Buddhist shrine – unlocks something unexpected and powerful in some of the pilgrims.
The last leg of their journey takes them along the spectacular north Wales coast path. They climb a steep pass through two peaks, known as the Rivals, before tackling a narrow muddy track high up on the cliffs. They come across another ancient church dedicated to St Beuno, which has straw covering the floor as well as a medieval lepers’ window.
On their penultimate day, the pilgrims reach Aberdaron, their final stop on the mainland. Here, they visit St Hywyn’s, a medieval church dedicated to the Celtic early Christian saint, and rich in pilgrim history. It’s a recent tradition that pilgrims collect a stone from the beach and then add it to a prayer stone cairn outside the church. But the process of ‘letting go’ unleashes waves of emotion in almost every pilgrim.

Covering an area almost the size of Spain but home to fewer than 50,000 people, the Yukon is a land of immense forests, glaciers, rivers and wildlife. In wealthy, modern Canada, Simon wants to find out how the people and the wildlife of this immense wilderness are faring - all while searching for an apex predator, the grizzly bear. programme.title: Inis na nIontas
programme.desc:
Sa chlár deiridh, tá Ardal i ndeisceart na tíre. Aimsíonn sé an t-oileán álainn Garinis, áit a bhfuil gairdíní lómhara agus an t-iolar bánearrach. Téann sé amach ar chadhc chun coilíneacht rónta a fheiceáil atá faoi bhláth sula mbogann sé ó dheas arís go hInis Arcáin, áit a dtéann sé amach ar an fharraige mhór chun ráth deilfeanna a fheiceáil. Insíonn staraí áitiúil dúinn faoi stair na bhfoghlaithe mara insan cheantar, agus nochtann ealaíontóir cónaitheach luach an oileáin mar thearmann do phéintéirí. Ní ghlacann sé i bhfad ar Ardal a bhealach a dhéanamh go Cléire, an t-oileán is faide ó dheas in Éirinn, áit a dtugann sé cuairt ar dhrioglann jin a bhfuil an cheilp mar bhunábhar ann. Idir an dá linn, buailimid le héaneolaí cónaitheach an oileáin a mhíníonn tábhacht an oileáin d’éin imirceacha. Aistear dá shaol a bhí ann d’Ardal.
In the final episode, Ardal is in the south, where he discovers beautiful Garnish Island, home to gorgeous, lush gardens and the rare white-tailed eagle. Travelling by kayak, Ardal sees the island's thriving seal colony, before heading south to Sherkin Island, where he is once again at sea and being introduced to a playful pod of dolphins. A local historian talks about the island’s pirate past, and a resident artist reveals its current status as a painters’ paradise.
A short hop takes Ardal to Cape Clear, Ireland’s southernmost island, where he is taken on a tour in one of the island’s electric buses. He is introduced to some remarkable standing stones and a gin distillery that uses foraged kelp. Meanwhile, we meet the island’s resident ornithologist, who explains the huge importance of the island for migratory birds. A climactic clifftop view, looking out across the Atlantic, marks the end to a revealing and unforgettable journey.

A year in the life of students attending courses with Gael Chúrsaí, a training college based in west Belfast. Its primary focus is to give young Irish language speakers an alternative path to education by offering them the opportunity to gain a qualification in a range of vocational skills like childcare, beauty, first aid, business finance and leadership.
In this first episode, college leader Colma Mhic Aoidh and her dedicated team of tutors confront one of their biggest challenges: relocating to a new facility. All the while, they’re maintaining the day-to-day function of the college, training and enrolling new students.
Tutor Ursula helps sort out the new beauty school and takes the first-ever cookery class in the college. Student Andrew is aiming to become a classroom assistant, and his course tutor Frances visits him in the classroom to assess how he’s progressing. Young music fanatic Ethan embarks upon a new adventure as he has ambitions of becoming a DJ and gets the opportunity to work alongside the team at Raidió Fáilte. programme.title: Finding Britain’s Slave Traders with David Olusoga
programme.desc:
David Olusoga meets the historians who have built the Register of British Slave Traders. For five years, they have searched through thousands of documents, piecing together a comprehensive picture of over 13,000 individuals who were investors in the slave trade. Anyone can now log on and discover who the slave traders were, where they lived, how much money they made and the links between modern British institutions and the trade in human beings.
David discovers how the monarchy drove the early British slave trade. He learns how Elizabeth I and the early Stuarts gave their support to early slavery ventures; how the restored monarchy in the 1660s, seeking new ways to strengthen its finances and authorities, chartered a joint-stock monopoly company dedicated to the trade in enslaved Africans; and how James II, the company's governor, becoming king led to the emergence of a new and rival set of companies and investors who would transform the slave trade. programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc:
Cambridge is home to two of the country’s most groundbreaking hospitals - Addenbrooke’s and Royal Papworth, where surgeons take on some of the most challenging medical cases in the UK.
In this second episode, Addenbrooke’s neurosurgeon Rod Laing performs what is probably the most difficult spinal operation there is: removing a slipped disc deep in the spine that is pressing on the spinal cord and threatening the patient with paralysis.
His patient, 65-year-old psychologist Colin, started having problems walking and was eventually diagnosed with a slipped disc in the thoracic or middle part of the spine. Colin discovered that if nothing was done, he could eventually become paralysed from the waist down and lose control over his bladder and bowel function. He also found that most surgeons refused to do the operation to remove the disc because of the high risk of paralysis during the procedure. His salvation came in the form of Rod Laing, who was prepared to take on the case.
The operation is so challenging because to reach the slipped thoracic disc, Rod must enter through the side of the chest and work his way deep into the body, avoiding important nerves and blood vessels as he makes his way to the spine. The hole that Rod must operate down is probably one of the deepest there are in surgery, with the instruments just long enough to reach the site of the disc. And when Rod reaches the disc, the risks are at their highest, as it is pressing against the spinal cord. He must remove it millimetre by millimetre without disturbing the cord, or else he risks paralysing Colin.
At Royal Papworth, consultant cardiothoracic surgeon Narain Moorjani is also operating at the edge of what is possible. His patient Gertrude is an active and vibrant 80-year-old who needs surgery on three of the four valves in her heart. An irregular heartbeat has caused two of these valves to become defective, so her heart does not pump enough blood around her body. Without the operation, her heart will fail, and Gertrude, who says she still feels 30 years old, does not want to sit around waiting for her life to end.
To operate on the valves, Narain needs to put Gertrude on heart bypass and stop her heart.

programme.title: The Fix
programme.desc:
In a town under real strain, two former addicts with criminal pasts run a church where people arrive daily seeking help with addiction, poverty, homelessness and mental ill health. The film follows Bishop Mick and Pastor Emma as they step into the problems others often walk away from, using their own experiences to try and support people through crisis, recovery and relapse.
At the heart of their work is Exodus, a faith-based recovery programme Emma and Mick have built, based on lived experience. Within this project, they try to offer not just support, but a chance for those struggling with addiction and trauma to turn their lives around.
The church relies on volunteers - often people who have just come through recovery themselves; like local hard man Daz, a semi-pro boxer who struggled for years with addiction until he found God and sobriety. Fresh from the Exodus recovery programme, Daz is considered ready to give back to his community. When not manning the front steps of the church, he can be found helping others as a mentor in the Exodus group. Often he invites in friends and people he knows from the town.
Change however, is rarely straightforward. As people come and go, the film captures the reality of helping those on the edge and explores what happens when a community steps in to support people who feel they have nowhere else to turn. Despite all the challenges, the congregation share warmth and many laughs along the way. Presenter - Rory Carson Producer - Rory Carson Director - Aaron Black.

And in Moelfre, north Wales, training night is interrupted by a dog owner whose beloved pet has jumped off a cliff. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to Bridgend as the show brings its charity shop challenge to south Wales. With just 60 minutes on the clock and £100 each, best friends Anum and Betti go head-to-head to see who can turn second-hand bargains into the biggest profit for charity.
Paired with expert thrifters Pete and Lola, the race begins across Bridgend’s high street, where hidden gems lurk among the rails and shelves. Anum is drawn to vintage bric-a-brac and collectibles, snapping up teapots, crockery and curios, while Betti focuses on fashion, spotting bold fabrics, statement pieces and high-end labels.
But not every bargain is what it seems. Early excitement over a Burberry outfit raises questions about authenticity, while a pair of striking Christian Louboutin trainers presents a serious dilemma – a potential goldmine or a costly mistake. With the clock ticking and budgets shrinking, both teams must decide how much risk they are willing to take.
Once the shopping frenzy ends, attention turns to transformation. Each contestant chooses one item to be upcycled by expert makers. Betti’s nursery curtains are reworked into a stylish wrap dress, while Anum’s plain wooden jewellery box is transformed into a vibrant, hand-painted statement piece, proving that creativity can dramatically boost value.
Then comes the ultimate test: the live-streamed auction. Nerves are jangling as Anum and Betti step into the spotlight, pitching their items to a live online audience. As bids rise and fall in real time, confidence and charm become just as important as the items themselves. Authenticity checks deliver last-minute twists, and a risky gamble could either decide the winner or wipe out a chunk of their budget.
By the end of a dramatic auction, the profits are counted, surprises are revealed, and one contestant emerges ahead. But the real winner is charity, with all proceeds donated to the contestants’ chosen causes.
Packed with jeopardy, big decisions and satisfying transformations, the visit to Bridgend is a lively, feel-good episode that celebrates second-hand style, creative thinking and the thrill of finding hidden value where others might not look.

On auction day, the atmosphere is electric. Polly proves to be a natural at salesmanship, even getting Joanna to model her upcycled jacket to drive up bids. programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc:
Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die.
As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated.
Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death.
Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales.
Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the creative heart of Hebden Bridge – a former mill town famed for its independent spirit and as a filming location for the BBC TV series Happy Valley.
Today’s competitors are friends Emma and Sophie, who first met on a fashion shoot for Dove House Hospice. Now they’re going head-to-head to raise as much money as possible for the charity that brought them together. Guiding them are expert vintage thrifters – and husbands – Tom and Terry.
The teams quickly reveal very different shopping styles. Sophie and Tom dive straight into the nearest shop, where Sophie’s love of oversized menswear leads her to a vintage St Michael jacket – a nostalgic find with added appeal thanks to its 'Made in the UK' label. Emma and Terry take a steadier approach, carefully assessing a rare red rotary dial telephone before building a collection packed with retro charm.
The hunt for Joanna’s pick of the day – an original 1970s Holly Hobbie doll – adds extra jeopardy. While Tom hesitates over the gamble, Sophie trusts her instinct and pushes to secure the collectable toy. As time slips away, Emma and Terry uncover a colourful 1960s picnic set and an eye-catching Murano-style glass duck that divides opinion but promises personality at auction.
For the upcycling challenge, creativity takes centre stage. Emma selects a vintage rocking chair and plans to re-cover it using fabric from animal-illustrated curtains – a bold, characterful refresh. Sophie, however, leaves her upcycle decision perilously late, eventually opting for an unexpected sleeping bag with plans to transform it into a statement padded coat.
The final minutes are frantic for Sophie and Tom, who scramble to spend the remainder of their budget. With Joanna urging them on, they squeeze in a last-second dash for additional vintage finds before they run out of time.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must swap browsing rails for the rostrum. Emma channels calm confidence, while Sophie leans into theatrical flair. With bids climbing and pride on the line, it’s a spirited showdown, but whatever the outcome, Dove House Hospice stands to benefit from a creative, chaotic and thoroughly entertaining day on Hebden Bridge's high street.

programme.title: Garden Rescue
programme.desc:
Chris and Lee travel to Eton Wick to help Andrew and Angela revive their Victorian cottage garden. Once lovingly maintained, it has now fallen into neglect, with a rotten pergola, a decaying arbour seat and overgrown borders in need of care. The uneven, rough surface also makes the garden unsafe and inaccessible for their young son William.
Andrew and Angela dream of putting their own twist on a traditional Victorian cottage garden with timeless tranquillity and modern functionality. They want to create a beautiful, low-maintenance space that’s also accessible for William, who relies on outdoor time because of his disabilities. The garden will feature smooth, accessible pathways, strategic seating areas and a calming, interactive play zone designed with William’s mobility in mind. A secluded corner filled with soothing plants and comfortable seating will offer the family a place to unwind and reconnect after hospital visits and busy days.
Andrew and Angela met while on holiday in Dublin and have shared a love of travel ever since. Angela, originally from America, and Andrew, a seasoned world traveller himself, settled down when she became pregnant, buying their home to start a family. But life soon took an unexpected turn when their son William was born prematurely with a rare condition, bilateral tibial hemimelia, causing severe malformations in both legs and feet. Their renovation plans were put on hold as hospital visits, surgeries and recoveries became part of everyday life. Earlier this year, William underwent an amputation of his right leg and is now learning to walk confidently with his prosthetic. Three further surgeries on his left leg are planned, with more likely into his early twenties.
Despite these challenges, Andrew and Angela remain optimistic and determined to create a safe, tranquil and joyful outdoor space where William can play and the family can relax together.
Can Chris and Lee craft a Victorian haven garden, one that blends charm, accessibility and serenity, on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Rose Ayling-Ellis came to fame on EastEnders and captured the nation’s hearts when she won Strictly. Since then, she’s used her platform to campaign for deaf rights. Now, Rose goes in search of her family history. She’s heard a rumour of Italian ancestry on her father’s side and is hoping for a bit of drama on her mum’s.
Rose starts by visiting her mum in Kent. Rose’s mum has an intriguing picture of Rose’s three-time great-grandmother. The family story is that she ran a pub in Birmingham with an iron fist. But Rose’s mum doesn’t know her name or if any of the stories are true. To find out, Rose heads to Birmingham.
Local historian Simon Briercliffe helps Rose put a name to her three-time great-grandmother – Agnes Chilton. Trade directories and census returns show that Agnes and her husband Alfred ran a pub. A local newspaper article tells a story worthy of an EastEnders plotline: Agnes and Alfred were caught up in an altercation with a customer, resulting in a court appearance. Rose discovers that Alfred died aged 48, leaving Agnes a widow. Fearing the worst for a woman on her own at that time, Rose is happy to discover that shortly after Alfred’s death Agnes moved to her own pub, the Aston Tavern.
Rose heads there to meet historian Professor Julie-Marie Strange and discovers that Agnes married again at the age of 50. However, two years later, Agnes’s second husband also died. Once again, Agnes was undeterred and expanded the pub further. Rose is delighted to find out that the current landlord of the Aston Tavern has named the rooms after former landlords, including Agnes. As Rose goes to find the room named after her ancestor, she reflects on what a resilient woman Agnes was.
Rose then turns to the paternal side of the family. At her dad’s house in Somerset, Rose’s grandma tells her that her father, Rose’s great-grandad, came from a huge family of 17 children. She doesn’t know a lot about them but remembers that her grandfather, James Welland, Rose’s great-great-grandad, lost his hand in an accident, and she also recalls her dad telling her that when he was a child, they were very poor and lived in a squat in Exeter. Rose also asks about the Italian connection. Rose’s dad explains that this story came through his dad’s side of the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads west to the seaside town of Aberystwyth, famous for its Victorian pier and unpredictable weather. Battling the rain are mother-and-son duo Margaret and Endaf, both hoping their shared love of a bargain will translate into serious profit for charity.
With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they’re paired with expert thrifters and sent racing around Aberystwyth’s charity shops. Endaf starts strongly, snapping up a quality blazer for under a tenner before confidently adding crystal glasses and rare Babycham glasses to his haul. He later spots a vintage wool-and-cashmere jacket, Joanna’s pick of the day, and takes a chance on a violin, proving he is willing to think outside the box.
Margaret, meanwhile, wastes no time securing her upcycle item – a nest of dark wood tables bought for just £3. She also picks up Dutch wooden clogs, a vintage leather messenger bag and gambles on an expensive suede jacket, carefully selecting items she believes have strong resale appeal. The contest has a warm but competitive family dynamic, with playful rivalry building between mum and son as the clock ticks down.
At the transformation stage, Endaf’s plain 80s leather jacket is dramatically reworked with fabric paint and new gold hardware by upcycle entrepreneur Emma Deeks, turning it into a bold statement piece. Margaret’s modest £3 tables are transformed by using a poured-paint technique, creating a colourful, marbled finish that completely reinvents them.
Then comes the live-streamed auction. Endaf grows in confidence as he pitches his items, using detail and humour to drive bids higher, especially on the vintage Burton jacket and his upcycled leather piece. Margaret charms viewers with her warmth and storytelling, successfully selling her clogs and making a strong profit on her upcycled tables.
When the totals are combined with their online sales, who will win between mother and son? The real triumph is for their chosen charity, the British Heart Foundation, with an impressive amount raised in total.
Rain-soaked, good-humoured and full of personality, this contest is a heartwarming family face-off that proves thrifting talent might just run in the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to Bridgend as the show brings its charity shop challenge to south Wales. With just 60 minutes on the clock and £100 each, best friends Anum and Betti go head-to-head to see who can turn second-hand bargains into the biggest profit for charity.
Paired with expert thrifters Pete and Lola, the race begins across Bridgend’s high street, where hidden gems lurk among the rails and shelves. Anum is drawn to vintage bric-a-brac and collectibles, snapping up teapots, crockery and curios, while Betti focuses on fashion, spotting bold fabrics, statement pieces and high-end labels.
But not every bargain is what it seems. Early excitement over a Burberry outfit raises questions about authenticity, while a pair of striking Christian Louboutin trainers presents a serious dilemma – a potential goldmine or a costly mistake. With the clock ticking and budgets shrinking, both teams must decide how much risk they are willing to take.
Once the shopping frenzy ends, attention turns to transformation. Each contestant chooses one item to be upcycled by expert makers. Betti’s nursery curtains are reworked into a stylish wrap dress, while Anum’s plain wooden jewellery box is transformed into a vibrant, hand-painted statement piece, proving that creativity can dramatically boost value.
Then comes the ultimate test: the live-streamed auction. Nerves are jangling as Anum and Betti step into the spotlight, pitching their items to a live online audience. As bids rise and fall in real time, confidence and charm become just as important as the items themselves. Authenticity checks deliver last-minute twists, and a risky gamble could either decide the winner or wipe out a chunk of their budget.
By the end of a dramatic auction, the profits are counted, surprises are revealed, and one contestant emerges ahead. But the real winner is charity, with all proceeds donated to the contestants’ chosen causes.
Packed with jeopardy, big decisions and satisfying transformations, the visit to Bridgend is a lively, feel-good episode that celebrates second-hand style, creative thinking and the thrill of finding hidden value where others might not look.

programme.title: Stacey Dooley
programme.desc:
Stacey Dooley looks into the deaths of women who have fallen from height, in cases where domestic abuse may have been part of the wider picture, and asks what role, if any, abuse can play in how these women die.
As Stacey meets bereaved families, survivors, detectives, lawyers and campaigners, she explores how coercive control can shape women’s lives long before a fatal incident, and whether those histories are given sufficient weight when deaths are investigated.
Among the cases, we see Stacey meet the family of Bianca Thomas, a young mother from Birmingham who died after falling from an 11th-floor balcony. Bianca's death was ruled accidental, but her family still have questions about the circumstances surrounding her death.
Stacey also hears about the landmark case of Kimberley Milne, whose husband was convicted in Scotland of culpable homicide after sustained domestic abuse was found to have been a significant contributing factor in her death by suicide, and asks what that could mean for similar cases in England and Wales.
Powerful and deeply personal, the programme explores grief, justice and the difficult questions surrounding women who die after falling from height. programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads to the creative heart of Hebden Bridge – a former mill town famed for its independent spirit and as a filming location for the BBC TV series Happy Valley.
Today’s competitors are friends Emma and Sophie, who first met on a fashion shoot for Dove House Hospice. Now they’re going head-to-head to raise as much money as possible for the charity that brought them together. Guiding them are expert vintage thrifters – and husbands – Tom and Terry.
The teams quickly reveal very different shopping styles. Sophie and Tom dive straight into the nearest shop, where Sophie’s love of oversized menswear leads her to a vintage St Michael jacket – a nostalgic find with added appeal thanks to its 'Made in the UK' label. Emma and Terry take a steadier approach, carefully assessing a rare red rotary dial telephone before building a collection packed with retro charm.
The hunt for Joanna’s pick of the day – an original 1970s Holly Hobbie doll – adds extra jeopardy. While Tom hesitates over the gamble, Sophie trusts her instinct and pushes to secure the collectable toy. As time slips away, Emma and Terry uncover a colourful 1960s picnic set and an eye-catching Murano-style glass duck that divides opinion but promises personality at auction.
For the upcycling challenge, creativity takes centre stage. Emma selects a vintage rocking chair and plans to re-cover it using fabric from animal-illustrated curtains – a bold, characterful refresh. Sophie, however, leaves her upcycle decision perilously late, eventually opting for an unexpected sleeping bag with plans to transform it into a statement padded coat.
The final minutes are frantic for Sophie and Tom, who scramble to spend the remainder of their budget. With Joanna urging them on, they squeeze in a last-second dash for additional vintage finds before they run out of time.
At the live-streamed auction, both friends must swap browsing rails for the rostrum. Emma channels calm confidence, while Sophie leans into theatrical flair. With bids climbing and pride on the line, it’s a spirited showdown, but whatever the outcome, Dove House Hospice stands to benefit from a creative, chaotic and thoroughly entertaining day on Hebden Bridge's high street.

They want to create a beautiful, low-maintenance space that’s also accessible for William, who relies on outdoor time because of his disabilities. The garden will feature smooth, accessible pathways, strategic seating areas and a calming, interactive play zone designed with William’s mobility in mind. A secluded corner filled with soothing plants and comfortable seating will offer the family a place to unwind and reconnect after hospital visits and busy days.
Andrew and Angela met while on holiday in Dublin and have shared a love of travel ever since. Angela, originally from America, and Andrew, a seasoned world traveller himself, settled down when she became pregnant, buying their home to start a family. But life soon took an unexpected turn when their son William was born prematurely with a rare condition, bilateral tibial hemimelia, causing severe malformations in both legs and feet. Their renovation plans were put on hold as hospital visits, surgeries and recoveries became part of everyday life. Earlier this year, William underwent an amputation of his right leg and is now learning to walk confidently with his prosthetic. Three further surgeries on his left leg are planned, with more likely into his early twenties.
Despite these challenges, Andrew and Angela remain optimistic and determined to create a safe, tranquil and joyful outdoor space where William can play and the family can relax together.
Can Chris and Lee craft a Victorian haven garden, one that blends charm, accessibility and serenity, on a £6,000 budget?

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.desc:
First into the barn are Mira Karavadra and her husband Suraj, who bring a 1970s portable record player, radio and tape deck once owned by Mira’s father. Purchased in Uganda in 1972, the device became a lifeline for Mira’s family as they fled Idi Amin’s expulsion of South Asians. Unable to take valuables or money, Mira’s father disguised his remaining cash by buying the music system, which later became central to the family’s gatherings as they rebuilt their lives in Yorkshire. Now silent, corroded and broken, the treasured player is entrusted to electronics expert Mark Stuckey, who must tackle battery corrosion, a missing mains lead, a broken tone arm and a failed transformer to bring the beloved machine back to life.
Next to arrive is Joe Riley from Kent, carrying his grandfather Tom’s signet ring. Originally crafted in 1932 as a wedding gift for Tom’s father, the ring bears the initials 'MC' for Mary Cummings, Joe’s great-grandmother. Tom wore the ring every day, becoming a father figure to Joe after his parents divorced. Now wafer-thin, cracked and too small to wear, the ring has been rejected by jewellers unwilling to risk repairing its hollow construction. Goldsmith Richard Talman takes on the challenge, reinforcing the fragile structure with a custom-made internal shim, carefully soldering and laser-welding the cracked top plate, and finally passing the ring to engraver Sam Marsden, who delicately restores Mary’s original initials before Richard has a chance to visit Joe and pass on some valuable tips on polishing such a precious item.
The third repair belongs to Rachel Twumasi-Corson, who brings her cherished Ghanaian djembe drum. Rachel spent her childhood travelling between London and Accra, where her grandfather, an influential political figure, encouraged her education. The drum, adorned with hand-carved patterns, a lion motif and traditional kente cloth, was bought during a meaningful visit to Elmina Castle. Over years of family use, church events and children’s play, the drum suffered marker-pen scribbles and a severe split in its wooden base.

programme.title: Who Do You Think You Are
programme.desc:
Rose Ayling-Ellis came to fame on EastEnders and captured the nation’s hearts when she won Strictly. Since then, she’s used her platform to campaign for deaf rights. Now, Rose goes in search of her family history. She’s heard a rumour of Italian ancestry on her father’s side and is hoping for a bit of drama on her mum’s.
Rose starts by visiting her mum in Kent. Rose’s mum has an intriguing picture of Rose’s three-time great-grandmother. The family story is that she ran a pub in Birmingham with an iron fist. But Rose’s mum doesn’t know her name or if any of the stories are true. To find out, Rose heads to Birmingham.
Local historian Simon Briercliffe helps Rose put a name to her three-time great-grandmother – Agnes Chilton. Trade directories and census returns show that Agnes and her husband Alfred ran a pub. A local newspaper article tells a story worthy of an EastEnders plotline: Agnes and Alfred were caught up in an altercation with a customer, resulting in a court appearance. Rose discovers that Alfred died aged 48, leaving Agnes a widow. Fearing the worst for a woman on her own at that time, Rose is happy to discover that shortly after Alfred’s death Agnes moved to her own pub, the Aston Tavern.
Rose heads there to meet historian Professor Julie-Marie Strange and discovers that Agnes married again at the age of 50. However, two years later, Agnes’s second husband also died. Once again, Agnes was undeterred and expanded the pub further. Rose is delighted to find out that the current landlord of the Aston Tavern has named the rooms after former landlords, including Agnes. As Rose goes to find the room named after her ancestor, she reflects on what a resilient woman Agnes was.
Rose then turns to the paternal side of the family. At her dad’s house in Somerset, Rose’s grandma tells her that her father, Rose’s great-grandad, came from a huge family of 17 children. She doesn’t know a lot about them but remembers that her grandfather, James Welland, Rose’s great-great-grandad, lost his hand in an accident, and she also recalls her dad telling her that when he was a child, they were very poor and lived in a squat in Exeter. Rose also asks about the Italian connection. Rose’s dad explains that this story came through his dad’s side of the family.

programme.title: Shift the Thrift
programme.desc:
Joanna Page heads west to the seaside town of Aberystwyth, famous for its Victorian pier and unpredictable weather. Battling the rain are mother-and-son duo Margaret and Endaf, both hoping their shared love of a bargain will translate into serious profit for charity.
With £100 each and just 60 minutes on the clock, they’re paired with expert thrifters and sent racing around Aberystwyth’s charity shops. Endaf starts strongly, snapping up a quality blazer for under a tenner before confidently adding crystal glasses and rare Babycham glasses to his haul. He later spots a vintage wool-and-cashmere jacket, Joanna’s pick of the day, and takes a chance on a violin, proving he is willing to think outside the box.
Margaret, meanwhile, wastes no time securing her upcycle item – a nest of dark wood tables bought for just £3. She also picks up Dutch wooden clogs, a vintage leather messenger bag and gambles on an expensive suede jacket, carefully selecting items she believes have strong resale appeal. The contest has a warm but competitive family dynamic, with playful rivalry building between mum and son as the clock ticks down.
At the transformation stage, Endaf’s plain 80s leather jacket is dramatically reworked with fabric paint and new gold hardware by upcycle entrepreneur Emma Deeks, turning it into a bold statement piece. Margaret’s modest £3 tables are transformed by using a poured-paint technique, creating a colourful, marbled finish that completely reinvents them.
Then comes the live-streamed auction. Endaf grows in confidence as he pitches his items, using detail and humour to drive bids higher, especially on the vintage Burton jacket and his upcycled leather piece. Margaret charms viewers with her warmth and storytelling, successfully selling her clogs and making a strong profit on her upcycled tables.
When the totals are combined with their online sales, who will win between mother and son? The real triumph is for their chosen charity, the British Heart Foundation, with an impressive amount raised in total.
Rain-soaked, good-humoured and full of personality, this contest is a heartwarming family face-off that proves thrifting talent might just run in the family.

programme.title: James May's Man Lab
programme.desc: James May attempts Man Lab's most secretive and risky stunt to date, which involves an ailing seaside town and a great big monster. Also, James challenges his hapless sidekick Rory to the unenviable task of running a whelk stall, a new type of table football is invented for every England fan, and a cup of tea will never be wasted again with the amazing `Cup of Tea Alarm'. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Toy Stories
programme.desc: James May is out to prove why traditional, old fashioned toys are still relevant today when he pushes them to the limit in spectacular, supersize challenges. James takes model aeroplanes to a whole new level when he tries to make a full size spitfire out of Airfix. But the venture soon hits problems when it becomes clear the giant 36 foot pieces may not be strong enough and nobody knows how they will fit together. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Toy Stories
programme.desc: James tries to make a garden entirely out of Plasticine and then enter it at the Chelsea Flower Show. He persuades thousands of members of the British public to help make the thousands of Plasticine flowers he needs, but will it be enough to persuade the guardians of the world's most prestigious horticultural event to let him make a garden with no real flowers in it. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Toy Stories
programme.desc: James joins forces with Edwina Currie to build a full-size bridge from nothing but Meccano. Top engineers pitch incredible designs, but the project soon careers out of control when the Meccano does not arrive and James realizes it will take longer to build than he ever imagined. A last-minute accident also means that James' bridge may never see the light of day. James May - Host.

programme.title: World at War
programme.desc: Despite having the largest pre-war European army, France's outdated forces were humiliated by the Germans. programme.sub-title: Cast Adrift ║ Documentary / Animals / Miniseries / Nature ║ 2016
programme.desc: Isolated since the time of the dinosaurs, New Zealand's wildlife has been left to its own devices - with surprising consequences. Its ancient forests are still stalked by predators from the Jurassic era. It's also one of the most geologically active countries on Earth. From Kiwis with their giant eggs, to forest-dwelling penguins and helicopter-riding sheep dogs, meet the astonishing creatures and resilient people who must rise to the challenges of their beautiful, dramatic and demanding home. Mark Flowers - Director Sam Neill - Narrator.

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.sub-title: Wild Extremes ║ Documentary / Animals / Miniseries / Nature ║ 2016
programme.desc: The most extreme and wild parts of New Zealand are in the South Island, which lie towards Antarctica, in the path of the tempestuous `roaring forties'. This is home to some of the most rapidly rising mountains in the world, the Southern Alps. From hyper-intelligent parrots, to sinister snails with teeth and magical constellations of glow-worms, this is the story of New Zealand's wildest places and its most resilient pioneers, all of who must embrace radical solutions to survive. Robert Morgenstern - Director Sam Neill - Narrator.

James takes model aeroplanes to a whole new level when he tries to make a full size spitfire out of Airfix. But the venture soon hits problems when it becomes clear the giant 36 foot pieces may not be strong enough and nobody knows how they will fit together. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Toy Stories
programme.desc: James tries to make a garden entirely out of Plasticine and then enter it at the Chelsea Flower Show. He persuades thousands of members of the British public to help make the thousands of Plasticine flowers he needs, but will it be enough to persuade the guardians of the world's most prestigious horticultural event to let him make a garden with no real flowers in it. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Toy Stories
programme.desc: James joins forces with Edwina Currie to build a full-size bridge from nothing but Meccano. Top engineers pitch incredible designs, but the project soon careers out of control when the Meccano does not arrive and James realizes it will take longer to build than he ever imagined. A last-minute accident also means that James' bridge may never see the light of day. James May - Host.

programme.title: James May's Man Lab

programme.title: World at War
programme.desc: Stricken by the humiliation of defeat and the harsh terms of the Treaty of Versailles, Germany looks to one man for a resurgence of hope and dignity - Adolf Hitler. David Elstein - Director Laurence Olivier - Narrator.

programme.title: World at War
programme.desc: While the full force of the Nazi war machine sweeps across Europe, an uneasy calm settles on Britain as Churchill replaces Chamberlain as prime minister. David Elstein - Director Laurence Olivier - Narrator Rab Butler Bernard Kops Robert Boothby.

programme.title: World at War
programme.desc: Despite having the largest pre-war European army, France's outdated forces were humiliated by the Germans. Identifying a weakness in the Maginot Line, a defensive border which ran along the north east of France but did not extend to the channel in the west, German air and armour power simply skirted the line in the north and forged south. David Elstein - Director Laurence Olivier - Narrator Edward Spears Lawrence Durrell Siegfried Westphal Gordon Waterfield.

programme.sub-title: Series 1 : The Nidd ║ Documentary / History / Nature / Outdoors ║ 2018
programme.desc: Blind adventurer Amar Latif takes a walk on a route along one of Yorkshire's most stunning river valleys. He abseils into a hidden gorge, canoes across a reservoir and meets the local llamas while following a riverside trail along the Nidd. Amar Latif - Host.

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.sub-title: Cast Adrift ║ Documentary / Animals / Miniseries / Nature ║ 2016
programme.desc: Isolated since the time of the dinosaurs, New Zealand's wildlife has been left to its own devices - with surprising consequences. Its ancient forests are still stalked by predators from the Jurassic era. It's also one of the most geologically active countries on Earth. From Kiwis with their giant eggs, to forest-dwelling penguins and helicopter-riding sheep dogs, meet the astonishing creatures and resilient people who must rise to the challenges of their beautiful, dramatic and demanding home. Mark Flowers - Director Sam Neill - Narrator.

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.sub-title: Wild Extremes ║ Documentary / Animals / Miniseries / Nature ║ 2016
programme.desc: The most extreme and wild parts of New Zealand are in the South Island, which lie towards Antarctica, in the path of the tempestuous `roaring forties'. This is home to some of the most rapidly rising mountains in the world, the Southern Alps. From hyper-intelligent parrots, to sinister snails with teeth and magical constellations of glow-worms, this is the story of New Zealand's wildest places and its most resilient pioneers, all of who must embrace radical solutions to survive. Robert Morgenstern - Director Sam Neill - Narrator.

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.sub-title: New Arrivals ║ Documentary / Animals / Miniseries / Nature ║ 2016
programme.desc: New Zealand was one of the last land-masses to be found and settled by people. Lush and fertile, almost everything brought here flourishes, often with surprising consequences. Told through the experiences of its native species - in particular, a charismatic and peculiar giant, flightless parrot - this is the moving story of the changing fortunes of New Zealand's wildlife, since humans first arrived. Robert Morgenstern - Director Sam Neill - Narrator.

programme.title: Wild Japan
programme.desc: The central island of Honshu is home to over 100 million people, but it has a wild heart - most of Honshu is mountainous. This wilderness is home to an astonishing range of wildlife. Michelle Dockery - Narrator.

programme.desc: The most extreme and wild parts of New Zealand are in the South Island, which lie towards Antarctica, in the path of the tempestuous `roaring forties'. This is home to some of the most rapidly rising mountains in the world, the Southern Alps. From hyper-intelligent parrots, to sinister snails with teeth and magical constellations of glow-worms, this is the story of New Zealand's wildest places and its most resilient pioneers, all of who must embrace radical solutions to survive. Robert Morgenstern - Director Sam Neill - Narrator.

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.sub-title: New Arrivals ║ Documentary / Animals / Miniseries / Nature ║ 2016
programme.desc: New Zealand was one of the last land-masses to be found and settled by people. Lush and fertile, almost everything brought here flourishes, often with surprising consequences. Told through the experiences of its native species - in particular, a charismatic and peculiar giant, flightless parrot - this is the moving story of the changing fortunes of New Zealand's wildlife, since humans first arrived. Robert Morgenstern - Director Sam Neill - Narrator.

programme.title: Wild Japan
programme.desc: The central island of Honshu is home to over 100 million people, but it has a wild heart - most of Honshu is mountainous. This wilderness is home to an astonishing range of wildlife. Michelle Dockery - Narrator.

programme.title: New Zealand: Earth's Mythical Islands
programme.sub-title: Cast Adrift ║ Documentary / Animals / Miniseries / Nature ║ 2016
programme.desc: Isolated since the time of the dinosaurs, New Zealand's wildlife has been left to its own devices - with surprising consequences. Its ancient forests are still stalked by predators from the Jurassic era. It's also one of the most geologically active countries on Earth. From Kiwis with their giant eggs, to forest-dwelling penguins and helicopter-riding sheep dogs, meet the astonishing creatures and resilient people who must rise to the challenges of their beautiful, dramatic and demanding home. Mark Flowers - Director Sam Neill - Narrator.

programme.sub-title: S7E17 ║ Pedal Plane, Cigar Box Ukulele and Little Zoo Animals ║ Diy, Arts And Crafts ║ GB ║ 2021
programme.desc: Metal maestro Dominic Chinea is blown away by a prewar ride-on toy aeroplane that has been grounded for decades. Owner Charlotte is hoping to restore her grandpa's vintage toy for her own daughter Phoebe to enjoy. Rusty and in pieces, getting the plane fit for piloting again is going to be a mammoth job for Dom. Jay Blades.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.sub-title: S7E18 ║ Salt and Pepper Pots, Talking Doll, WW2 Pow Hat ║ Diy, Arts And Crafts ║ GB ║ 2021
programme.desc: Silversmith Brenton West takes on the repair of a salt and pepper music box of great sentimental value to owner Janice. The ornate pair was purchased in Hong Kong by Janice's mother, who accompanied her father during his army posting in the 1950s. Janice played with the set throughout her childhood, and now she wants her daughter to treasure it for future generations. Jay Blades.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.sub-title: S7E19 ║ Pocket Camera, Piglet and Marble Stone ║ Diy, Arts And Crafts ║ GB ║ 2021
programme.desc: Camera restorer Brenton West tackles a vintage pocket camera, believed to have taken the final photo of a loving family before they dispersed following their mother's death. Owner Geoff cherishes this prized possession that has been in the family since the early 1900s. Toy restorers Amanda Middleditch and Julie Tatchell get to grips with a stuffed pig that is crying out for some TLC. Jay Blades.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.sub-title: S7E20 ║ Mum's Trophy, Father's Bird Cage and Boxing Bag ║ Diy, Arts And Crafts ║ GB ║ 2021
programme.desc: Silversmith Brenton West is tasked with reviving a worn-down singing trophy that celebrates the musical talent of a sadly departed mother. Won in 1955, it commemorates a young girl who turned her back on singing when she started a family. With one handle missing and the silver plate tarnished and dented, the trophy is in bad shape. Jay Blades.

programme.title: The Repair Shop
programme.sub-title: S7E21 ║ Chesterfield Armchair, Brass Box, Silver Bracelet ║ Diy, Arts And Crafts ║ GB ║ 2021
programme.desc: Jay Blades and the team bring three treasured family heirlooms, and the memories they hold, back to life. First through the barn doors is Gloria Bartlett. She's brought her pride and joy, a Chesterfield armchair, in the hope that upholstery superstar Sonnaz Norranvary can return it to mint condition. She borrowed the money to pay for two chairs and a sofa in the 1980s and at the time felt very extravagant. Jay Blades.

programme.title: Help! My House is Haunted
programme.desc: The team investigate reports of paranormal activity in a pub in Calverton, but soon learn that strange phenomena are happening all over the historic village. Chris Fleming Barri Ghai Sandy Lakdar.

programme.title: Help! My House is Haunted
programme.sub-title: S3E1 ║ A Sinister Attachment ║ Paranormal, Reality ║ GB ║ 2021
programme.desc: Daniel and Claire believe renovations on their home have stirred a residual energy. The team investigate whether Claire has a demonic attachment, and if there is anything they can do to rid the house of the Demon. Chris Fleming Barri Ghai Sandy Lakdar.

programme.title: Help! My House is Haunted
programme.sub-title: S3E3 ║ The Ghost of Gertie ║ Paranormal, Reality ║ GB ║ 2021
programme.desc: The Bull Hotel dates back to the 14th century and is said to be a hotbed of paranormal activity. The team investigate a child spirit that's been scaring the staff, and making them worried to work there. Chris Fleming Barri Ghai Sandy Lakdar.

programme.desc: Gopal's happy marriage with Radha begins to crumble when she reconnects with her friend Suraj and becomes consumed by his music career. Doubt and jealousy drive Gopal to walk away from her.

programme.title: Bbuddah Hoga Terra Baap
programme.desc: Vijju, an ex-convict called from Paris to kill ACP Karan Malhotra, meets his old love and estranged wife, leading him to leave behind his dark past and criminal life.

programme.title: Hungama
programme.desc: A wealthy village businessman moves to the bustling city with his wife, only to trigger hilarious chaos after getting caught in a complex case of mistaken identity.

programme.title: De Dana Dan
programme.desc: Two broke friends, eager to marry their girlfriends, hatch a plan to kidnap a rich woman's pet for ransom, but their quick-money scheme soon spirals into chaos.

programme.title: Filler
programme.desc: A short interstitial programme providing brief entertainment, information or visual content between scheduled shows, helping maintain continuity throughout the channel's programming.

programme.title: Takkar
programme.desc: Photographer Ravi Malhotra is framed by corrupt cop D'Costa just before his wedding. While imprisoned, he studies law, plotting revenge and preparing to confront the man who ruined his life.

programme.title: Ram Jaane
programme.desc: Ram Jaane, an orphan who becomes a feared criminal, is urged by his social worker friend to change his ways. But he cares more about winning Bela's love than choosing a better path in life.

programme.title: Dashing Cm Bharath
programme.desc: Bharat, an Oxford graduate, becomes chief minister after his father's death. Determined to fight corruption, he faces fierce resistance and obstacles from powerful enemies.

programme.title: Joroo Ka Ghulam
programme.desc: Rajesh pretends to be wealthy to impress Kalpana and her family, leading to a series of comic situations and misunderstandings.

programme.title: Khoobsurat (1999)
programme.desc: Sanju, desperate to save himself and Gudia, poses as an NRI relative to swindle money from the Chaudharys, but finds more than he bargained for inside their home.

programme.title: Soldier
programme.desc: After Major Vijay Malhotra's colleagues betray him, he is branded as a traitor and subsequently killed. But his son, Vicky, vows to take revenge on his father's murderers and prove his innocence.

programme.title: Yeh Jawani Hai Deewani
programme.desc: Naina, a studious girl, yearns for some fun. A chance meeting with an old classmate, Aditi, leads to a trip that changes her life forever. She meets and falls for Bunny, but he has no time for love.

programme.title: Kambakkht Ishq
programme.desc: Simrita, a doctor, operates on Viraj, whom she dislikes. She accidentally leaves her watch inside his and must fix the mistake before her career and life fall apart.

programme.title: Mahaan
programme.desc: A lawyer hides after being falsely accused. His wife gives birth to twins. Years later, fate reunites the family under painful but healing circumstances. Love finds its way back.

programme.title: Romeo Akbar Walter
programme.desc: A bank cashier, Romeo, is recruited by India's intelligence agency for espionage in Pakistan. However, he finds himself in challenging situations when his cover gets blown.

programme.title: I Proud to Be an Indian
programme.desc: An Indian man travels to London for a family wedding, only to discover his community under threat from a racist group; compelled to act, he joins the fight to protect them and restore dignity.

programme.title: Sohni Mahiwal
programme.desc: Mirza falls in love with Sohni, daughter of a potter but their relationship is not accepted and he is thrown out of the town. Later, he then starts meeting her disguised as a shepherd.

programme.title: Hum Dil De Chuke Sanam
programme.desc: A newlywed learns his wife loves another man and selflessly decides to reunite them. Undeterred by judgment, he takes her to Italy to help her find true happiness with the one she truly loves.

programme.title: Awara Paagal Deewana
programme.desc: Dr. Anmol, a dentist stuck in a miserable marriage, sees his life turn worse when he unknowingly gets caught in the middle of a dangerous mafia rivalry in New York.
During India's partition, young Lenny and her caretaker Shanta are torn apart. Amid chaos, Shanta's love is tested as their fragile futures hang in balance together.

programme.title: U Me Aur Hum
programme.desc: While on a cruise, Dr Ajay Mehra falls in love with Piya and soon marries her. They lead a harmonious life until Piya gets pregnant and is soon diagnosed with Alzheimer's disease.

programme.title: Ansoo Ban Gaye Phool
programme.desc: Honest Vidyanand is jailed by a vengeful Seth. Humiliated, he vows revenge and is ready to go to any length to settle the score and reclaim his honor.

programme.title: Gippi
programme.desc: Gippi, an overweight teen, battles body image issues and social pressures while navigating adolescence. Through self-discovery, she learns to embrace her flaws and love herself unconditionally.

programme.title: Gori Tere Pyaar Mein
programme.desc: Sriram, a selfish and carefree man, deceives his girlfriend Dia for personal benefit. When guilt strikes, he tries to make amends and must meet Dia's condition to prove his love and earn forgiveness.

programme.title: Aatank (1996)
programme.desc: A coastal village finds black pearls in the sea, but their greed turns deadly when a fierce man-eating shark rises from the ocean's depths to protect its home.

programme.title: Rocky Aur Rani Kii Prem Kahaani
programme.desc: Rocky, a Punjabi, falls in love with Rani, a Bengali journalist. Facing strong family opposition, they decide to live with each other's families for three months to prove their love before marriage.

programme.title: Happy New Year
programme.desc: Charlie forms a team of misfits to rob a Dubai hotel under the guise of entering a dance competition held there. With help from a skilled bar dancer, they plan a daring and entertaining heist.

programme.title: Boss
programme.desc: After being disowned by his father, a businessman raises Surya as his own. Years later, Surya becomes Boss, fighting for the rights of society's deprived and oppressed, seeking justice and change.
